articles.title: 100 influencers invited to US Open spark debate on 'tennis etiquette'
articles.summary: The behaviour of influencers and content creators has become a major talking point at this year's US Open amid incidents of matches being disrupted.

blocks.text: Lights. Camera. Quiet please...
When it comes to etiquette in tennis, there are a fair few unwritten rules.
Apologising after winning a point from a net cord. Honesty around line calls, double bounces and double-hits. Post-match handshakes.
As for the spectators, it is common courtesy not to disturb the players during points.
Around 100 influencers and content creators have been granted accreditation for the tournament in New York - double the amount from last year.
Their presence has led to debate over how to balance bringing tennis to a new, different audience while respecting the game's etiquette.
"I definitely think it's cool to have a new demographic and I definitely think it helps grow the sport," world number four Coco Gauff said.
"But if you're being invited to a red carpet, you wouldn't show up in jeans.
"I think it's just follow the etiquette of the sport. That's all."
During two-time champion Naomi Osaka's first-round match on Arthur Ashe Stadium, one group held a photo shoot in their hospitality suite while play was going on.
The group turned on a portable ring light while Osaka was serving, leading to a reprimand from the umpire.
When Osaka returned on Thursday, the umpire had to remind the crowd several times to be quiet.
"Today the umpire told everyone to be quiet more than I've ever heard an umpire tell a crowd to be quiet," Osaka said.
"I tell people I normally just focus on the match and the court, but there was a moment where there was people shouting and you could hear it quite clearly.
"I think it bothered my opponent, too."
In one video, which has gone viral, a group can be seen speaking loudly as they film themselves during Osaka's first-round match on Tuesday, which led to the chair umpire calling for them to stop.
"I think obviously if you come to a sporting event, you have to respect the sport," Osaka said.
"I feel like it's common courtesy to read up on the sport, especially the etiquette.

"It could be a good thing for people to make the sport of tennis popular to their specific audience, but I think it has to be managed a lot better, especially in the situation like my first-round match.
"Overall, I think there are huge positives. You want people to continue to grow the sport.
"I just think it has to be in a way that everyone knows the rules and the etiquette."
Arthur Ashe is the biggest tennis stadium in the world, and matches are often accompanied by a buzz of noise from conversations around the arena.
Some players love it. Some do not.
Men's seventh seed Daniil Medvedev, who has had a tricky relationship with the New York crowds in the past, believes whatever brings more eyes to tennis can only be a good thing.
"I think the more we try to raise awareness about tennis, the better it is, the more popular the sport is," the Russian said.
"The more the sport grows, the better it is. I trust USTA [tournament organisers the United States Tennis Association] with what they are doing.
"I think [there is] a lot more upside than downside, so go for it."
American 11th seed Frances Tiafoe praised the diversity of the crowd in New York.
"I think the Open is great because you get all types of people that want to come and watch tennis," he said.
"All different walks of life, different types of people, different type of occupations. Personally, I love that.
"I have no problem with anybody doing anything, coming to watch the tennis."
American world number three Jessica Pegula, however, said some of the behaviour had been "disrespectful".
"I can appreciate the influencers coming and showcasing the US Open experience," Pegula said.
"But I do think that it's tough when you see videos when they're taking pictures and using the selfie lights.
"People are down there trying to perform. It's their career and their job. It seems a bit disrespectful.
"I think it's become a little too much this year.
"I can appreciate one side of it, but I think when you have the other side literally interrupting matches, it gets a little tough."
The US Open introduced a policy of free fan movement in 2024, meaning fans no longer have to wait to take their seats during changeovers.

A year later, the tournament was expanded to 15 days. The week before the singles draw is now marketed as a 'Fan Week', showcasing the revamped mixed doubles competition and exhibition matches between players past and present.
It is all part of what tournament chief executive Craig Tiley hopes will become "the tennis Disneyland".

Tiley, asked about influencers being accredited in a pre-tournament news conference, said: "We need to find ways of reaching new audiences, reaching people in a way that they connect with media today.
"The creation of the creator credential has been a key part of that because it's enabled us to talk to people in a way that they're listening. That's been a big focus."

Since the incident in Osaka's first match, there has been increased messaging on screens around the ground reminding people to "refrain from any activity that could disrupt the game, including noise levels, flash photography and ring lights".
The USTA said in a statement it "is always striving to grow tennis in this country and bring new audiences into the sport".
"We want all of our fans and guests to have an incredible time when they attend, but we also need to ensure they do not interfere with the action and competition on the court," it added.
"We are continually looking for ways to ensure fans in the stands know what is permitted and what is prohibited."

articles.title: Labor groups: After steel plant raids, Filipino plant workers remain displaced
articles.summary: Around 900 workers lost jobs or income after government raids.

blocks.text: September 4, 2026 | 3:16pm

MANILA, Philippines — Labor groups are pressing the government to assist around 900 workers displaced after authorities shut down three steel plants in Luzon and Mindanao over alleged safety, labor and regulatory violations.

In separate statements, labor groups raised alarm over the lack of immediate assistance for an estimated over 900 workers left jobless, following the government’s raids in the steel plants of Pampanga, Misamis Oriental, and Davao City.

While law enforcement agencies cited regulatory violations— including the presence of undocumented foreign workers, who are mostly Chinese nationals, the illegal possession and use of radioactive industrial materials, and the production of substandard steel — labor groups stressed that local employees are bearing the brunt of the crackdown.
Kilusang Mayo Uno Southern Mindanao said workers affected by the Davao operation were left with little clarity or immediate support after the plant was shut down.
Across the three plants in Misamis Oriental, Pampanga and Davao City, workers have lost jobs or income as authorities investigate the alleged violations, the group said.

"Rather than feeling rescued, workers described experiencing fear, intimidation, and uncertainty. More troubling is what happened after the raid: the same government agencies that claimed to have acted in the workers' interest provided no immediate assistance, livelihood support, or clear plan for the hundreds of employees who suddenly lost their jobs and source of income," the group added.
DOLE urged to take lead
Employers may face investigation for the alleged violations, but workers should not become "collateral damage," Federation of Free Workers President Sonny Matula told Philstar.com.
Matula's group has urged the Department of Labor and Employment to determine what wages, benefits, livelihood assistance or alternative employment should be provided to affected workers.
"Sa workplace safety, hindi puwedeng kanya-kanyang inspeksyon at kanya-kanyang diskarte," Matula said.

(When it comes to workplace safety, agencies cannot just conduct separate inspections and follow their own approaches. The law puts DOLE at the center of OSH enforcement and inter-agency coordination.)

Republic Act 11058, or the Occupational Safety and Health Law, gives the labor secretary visitorial and enforcement powers over workplace safety standards. It also requires DOLE to establish mechanisms for coordination with other government agencies.

"That is why we are humbly asking Labor Secretary Francis Tolentino to take the lead. Maraming ahensiya ang maaaring tumulong, pero dapat malinaw kung sino ang nasa manibela. Sa kaligtasan ng manggagawa, coordination is not bureaucracy—it can save lives," Matula added.

(That is why we are humbly asking Labor Secretary Francis Tolentino to take the lead. Many agencies can help, but it must be clear who is at the wheel. When it comes to worker safety, coordination is not bureaucracy—it can save lives.)

Steel plants raided. Authorities conducted a series of raids on steel plants in Misamis Oriental, Pampanga and Davao City this year that uncovered alleged immigration, labor, and safety violations, as well as the use of radioactive-bearing materials and the manufacture of substandard steel products.

The operations began with a May 2026 raid on the Philippine Sanjia Steel Corporation in Tagoloan, Misamis Oriental, where 69 Chinese nationals and one Filipino were arrested; and continued with a July 19, operation at Chuang Xing Steel Corporation in Magalang, Pampanga, which led to the arrest of several Chinese nationals and one Filipino and the later cancellation of six Chinese workers’ employment permits.
In August 2026, authorities then raided the Davao Mighty Steel Corp. in Davao City, where 10 Chinese nationals and four Filipinos were taken into custody.
About the radioactive materials, Matula told Philstar.com, that 100 workers initially examined reportedly showed no acute symptoms.
"This does not eliminate the need for continuing medical monitoring," Matula said.

articles.title: FDA acting chief grilled over appointment, ties to predecessor Teston
articles.summary: The Food and Drug Administration's acting chief faced pointed questions on Friday, September 4, over how he got the post, after Sen. Raffy Tulfo linked his appointment to a controversial predecessor.

blocks.text: September 4, 2026 | 3:14pm

Food and Drug Administration Officer-in-Charge Franklin Tabaquin responds to Sen. Raffy Tulfo's questions about his credentials and his rise in the agency, following criticism of his predecessor, former FDA chief Paolo Teston.
Screengrab via Senate of the Philippines livestream

MANILA, Philippines — The Food and Drug Administration's acting chief faced pointed questions on Friday, September 4, over how he got the post, after Sen. Raffy Tulfo linked his appointment to a controversial predecessor.

Tulfo, who separately raised concerns about medicine procurement at the same hearing on the health department's proposed 2027 budget, told newly appointed Health Secretary Edwin Mercado he was not to blame for those issues.
The senator claimed the problems traced back to holdovers from the tenure of former Health Secretary Teodoro Herbosa.
One of those holdovers, Tulfo said, was former FDA Director General Paolo Teston, who left the post after being appointed as a new associate justice at the Court of Tax Appeals in late July.

Teston led the FDA as director general starting in mid-2025 after serving as health undersecretary. Tulfo has criticized his leadership since at least January, when he and fellow senators grilled Teston over the agency's failure to stop the sale of fake and unregistered medicine online.
But Tulfo then turned to someone else in the hearing room: Franklin Tabaquin, the FDA's current officer-in-charge, whom Tulfo claimed Teston had personally brought into the agency.

Herbosa led the health department before Jose "Brix" Pujalte Jr. and then Mercado took over in August. DOH employees have filed complaints alleging conflicts of interest tied to procurement during Herbosa's tenure.
Tulfo during Friday's hearing asked Tabaquin how he had entered the FDA. Tabaquin said he had come from the private sector and another government agency before applying for a position at the agency.
Asked who had recommended him, Tabaquin confirmed it was Teston.

Tulfo also asked Tabaquin to confirm he had skipped over more senior officials in his rise through the agency, and that he had a pending graft and corruption case before the Office of the Ombudsman. Tabaquin confirmed both.

Tabaquin said the case concerned delays that happened "way, way before my time." He said he became OIC deputy director for operations last October, was made deputy director general this July, and has served as officer-in-charge for only two weeks so far.
Tulfo argued that more experienced FDA staff had been passed over for the post.
"I don't know you. Okay? And there's nothing personal to what I'm going to say to you. You don't deserve to be the director general because there are others who are better than you," Tulfo said.
"Nagkamali ang Malacañang. Kasi binitbit ka ni Teston. Kung saan impyerno ka nanggaling, binitbit ka ni Teston," Tulfo said.
(Malacañang made a mistake. Because Teston brought you along. Wherever the hell you came from, Teston brought you along.)
Tulfo claimed he had received information that Tabaquin was being lined up to be named the FDA's permanent director general, a move he said would extend Teston's influence over the agency.
"The nonsense Teston was doing while he was still there just continues," Tulfo said of Tabaquin's appointment. — Cristina Chi

articles.title: Farage aides step down after undercover report on Reform UK donations
articles.summary:
James Orr and Dan Jukes have stepped down from positions pending outcome of party investigation, says Reform UK

Two key aides to Nigel Farage have stepped down from their roles pending the…

blocks.text: Two key aides to Nigel Farage have stepped down from their roles pending the outcome of an investigation by Reform UK into a broadcast by Channel 4 News alleging they breached political donation rules, a party spokesperson said.
James Orr and Dan Jukes are alleged to have breached donation rules by having polling paid for by an overseas company.
A report by Channel 4 News claimed Reform took funding from a US firm for three polls it commissioned earlier this year costing £32,500.
The purported donors were in fact undercover reporters from investigative group Verbatim posing as an American financier and his UK-based son.
Jukes, a senior aide to party leader Farage, and Orr, head of policy at Reform UK, were implicated in the allegations.
The spokesperson said: “Reform UK has launched an investigation following the broadcast of a Channel 4 News programme.
“Both individuals involved have stepped down from their respective positions pending the outcome of the investigation.
“The party believes it is important that the investigation is allowed to proceed independently and without prejudice. No further comment will be made while the investigation is ongoing.”

articles.title: ICYMI: Sara Duterte impeachment trial Week 9 highlights
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Former Department of Education chief of staff Michael Poa, now part of Vice President Sara Duterte’s defense team, was declared a hostile witness for the prosecution as the…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Former Department of Education chief of staff Michael Poa, now part of Vice President Sara Duterte’s defense team, was declared a hostile witness for the prosecution as the Senate impeachment court examined how P112.5 million in confidential funds was spent during Duterte’s tenure as education secretary.
His testimony on Day 21 on Sept. 2 followed two Philippine Army officers who questioned DepEd’s use of military certifications to justify its confidential fund expenses.
The prosecution, meanwhile, is weighing whether to drop the bribery allegations under Article III to speed up the trial and proceed to the unexplained wealth allegations under Article II.

The developments came as senator-judges also discussed the 16-vote threshold for conviction or acquittal, while the Senate adjusted its schedule to accommodate impeachment proceedings alongside budget hearings and plenary sessions.
Key developments

items: Col. Manaros Boransing II testified that the Philippine Army received no regular or confidential funds from Duterte’s offices for the 2023 Youth Leadership Summit and Information Education Communication activities.
Col. Magtangol Panopio said his certification only confirmed that the Army conducted youth summits in its area of operations and did not validate how DepEd spent its confidential funds.
Panopio said he personally considered it improper for DepEd to use his certification to support its confidential fund liquidation.
Both officers said they were shocked to learn during a House committee hearing in October 2024 that DepEd had cited Army programs to justify its confidential fund expenses.

Presiding Officer Francis Escudero barred witnesses from bringing earpieces, mobile phones, smartwatches and similar communication devices while testifying after the court determined that a viral image allegedly showing a witness wearing an earpiece was AI-generated.
Sen. Vicente Sotto III said names appearing on acknowledgment receipts can be considered aliases only if there is a real person behind them. Otherwise, they should be treated as fictitious names.
The Senate impeachment court declared Poa a hostile witness for the prosecution, allowing prosecutor Benjamin Tolosa Jr. to ask leading questions.
Poa was called to testify on the disbursement of P112.5 million in DepEd confidential funds during Duterte’s tenure as education secretary from 2022 to 2024.
Defense lead counsel Sheila Sison criticized the prosecution’s 13-point offer of testimony, saying it sounded like rhetoric intended to add drama to the proceedings.

Poa acknowledged that he could potentially face personal liability if Duterte is found guilty of misusing confidential funds, but maintained that he had no personal knowledge of how the money was spent.
He said he only learned during a House committee hearing in October 2024 that confidential funds had been handed to officials of the Vice Presidential Security and Protection Group.
Poa also confirmed that not a single peso from DepEd’s confidential funds went to the military’s Youth Leadership Summits.
The court reprimanded lawyers over a prolonged exchange during Poa’s testimony, with Escudero urging them to avoid wasting time.
Outside the court, the prosecution panel said it was considering dropping Article III, which covers alleged bribery involving DepEd procurement officials, to expedite the impeachment trial.
Lead public prosecutor Rep. Gerville Luistro said no final decision had been made but that proceeding directly to Article II, the unexplained wealth allegations, was being seriously considered.
Rep. Joel Chua said dropping the article would be a matter of prioritization rather than weakness, citing a similar move during the impeachment trial of former Chief Justice Renato Corona.

The prosecution also received bank documents and tax records involving Duterte, her husband Manases Carpio and associated companies. Rep. Terry Ridon described these as the final key pillar of evidence for the unexplained wealth allegations.
Senate Majority Leader Juan Miguel Zubiri confirmed that some senator-judges had discussed the possibility of revisiting the 16-vote threshold needed to convict or acquit Duterte.
The Senate also approved a scheduling arrangement allowing budget hearings and plenary sessions to proceed alongside afternoon impeachment proceedings.
Escudero separately floated holding whole-day impeachment sessions in October, with the trial potentially suspended in November to make way for the Senate’s legislative calendar. /dp

articles.title: Nepal: Two pulled alive from tunnel nine days after floods
articles.summary: Crews are racing to find hundreds more people still believed to be trapped after a glacier collapse triggered floods that killed more than 1,200 people.

image.caption: Rescue workers are racing to find hundreds of people still missing in the aftermath of the floods in NepalImage: Athit Perawongmetha/REUTERS

blocks.text: Rescuers in Nepal pulled two workers alive from a hydropower tunnel Friday, nine days after catastrophic floods swept through the country's border region with China.
Emergency teams are continuing efforts to reach hundreds more believed trapped inside similar tunnels.

The men, identified as mechanical foreman Sanjay Shah and mechanical supervisor Kabir Maharjan, were freed from the Upper Trishuli 3A Hydropower Station's tunnel along the Trishuli River, according to a statement from the office of Energy Minister Biraj Bhakta Shrestha.

"As long as there is breath, there is hope!" Shrestha said in a statement. "Rescue operations are continuing in all the affected tunnels. Let everyone's efforts and prayers continue. We have not lost hope."
What do we know about the rescue?
Rescuers first heard voices from inside the tunnel Friday morning, authorities said.

blocks.caption: The two survivors rescued from the Upper Trishuli 3A hydropower project were flown to KathmanduImage: Athit Perawongmetha/REUTERS

blocks.text: Video and photos showed Maharjan, 45, pulled from a hole in the ground as bystanders cheered. Images showed him being placed on a stretcher, while Shah, 30, whose face was covered in mud, was carried out on a worker's back to a rescue tent, where army doctors fitted him with an oxygen mask and checked his vitals.
An aide to the energy minister said Maharjan could not move his hands or legs, while Shah's injuries were not considered critical. Both men were flown to a hospital in Kathmandu.

Family members reacted with relief. Amir Maharjan, Kabir's brother, told the Associated Press, "I can't explain what we are feeling at the moment. We are just grateful to god," adding that the family was heading to the hospital to see him.
What is happening at the hydropower project sites?

These were the first successful rescues concerning the hydropower projects along the Trishuli River. Officials say as many as 900 workers remain missing across a number of project sites, with roughly 500 believed trapped in tunnels, according to local authorities.
Nepal floods trap hundreds in hydropower tunnels
At the Trishuli 3A project specifically, the Independent Power Producers Association of Nepal put the number of missing workers at 557, with about 115 believed trapped in the main tunnel.
Nepal's communication minister, Bikram Timilsina, said officials remained hopeful more survivors would be found: "We are waiting for the rescue of more and more people," he said.
A team of experts coordinating through a WhatsApp group has been guiding rescue crews at the sites, becoming a key tool alongside helicopters and heavy machinery in the search effort.
What is the scale of damage caused by the Nepal floods?

Separately, Nepal's disaster authority estimated the floods caused at least 387.5 billion Nepalese rupees ($2.56 billion, €2.20 billion) in damage to property, housing and infrastructure, Dharma Raj Upreti, chief of the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority, told Reuters.
He said the first four months of early recovery — including rebuilding roads, setting up temporary shelters, and restoring water and power — would cost an estimated $52.6 million.

"These are estimated amounts. We have calculated this in coordination with different concerned agencies and departments," Upreti said, noting a more detailed assessment would follow. He said Nepal would need to rebuild around 20,000 houses in flood-affected areas, with at least 7,500 destroyed outright.
After Nepal floods, survivors return to ruins of their homes
The floods on August 26 were triggered by the collapse of a glacier upstream on the Trishuli River that sent a wall of ice, rock and mud through towns and villages near the Nepal-China border.
At least 1,259 people have been killed in Nepal, according to the country's disaster management agency, with more than 5,000 still missing.
China reported 21 deaths and 541 people missing on the Tibet side of the border as of late Wednesday.

articles.title: Warrant out: Sara Duterte facing arrest in grave threats case
articles.summary: (2nd update) The vice president is facing an arrest over three counts of grave threats, with bail set for each count.

blocks.text: September 4, 2026 | 2:50pm

MANILA, Philippines (2nd update, 3:49 p.m.) — Vice President Sara Duterte is now facing arrest for having mentioned involving a hitman supposedly targeting President Ferdinand Marcos Jr, First Lady Liza Araneta Marcos and then-speaker Martin Romualdez.
Quezon City Regional Trial Court Branch 98 issued the warrant on Friday, September 4, for three counts of grave threats.
The court set bail at P120,000 for each count.
The Department of Justice said the court also denied Duterte's "Motion to Defer the Issuance of or Recall Arrest Warrant and Quash the Information."
In the same resolution, the court found probable cause to hold Duterte for trial on all three counts of grave threats and ordered the issuance of the arrest warrant, according to the DOJ.
"The Department respects the Court's ruling and reaffirms its commitment to the rule of law," the DOJ said.
Served
Duterte, in a statement, said her office received the warrant Friday.

"I confirm that I was given notice of a warrant of arrest dated September 4, 2026 issued by Judge Maria Angelica De Ramos of Branch 98, Quezon City and served by PNP Col Christine Tabdi in the Office of the Vice President. My lawyers Attys Paul Lim and Clifford Chua will attend to this matter immediately," she said.
Lim, Duterte's counsel, said the vice president and her team will exhaust legal remedies available to them.
"Regardless of the question on jurisdiction, she has no intention of evading the law and will continue to exercise all her legal remedies," Lim's statement read.
It was not immediately clear whether Duterte would turn herself in in response to the warrant.

Prosecutors filed the complaint against Duterte on August 11, amid her ongoing Senate impeachment trial. The filing stemmed from findings that the National Bureau of Investigation forwarded to the DOJ in February 2025.
The threats Duterte made during online press conferences in October and December 2024 also formed part of Article IV of the articles of impeachment against her.

articles.title: Labor leader urges DOLE to take role in steel plant raids
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — A labor leader has urged the Department of Labor and Employment to play a part in the government’s operations on steel plants with alleged violations, citing the welfare of the…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — A labor leader has urged the Department of Labor and Employment to play a part in the government’s operations on steel plants with alleged violations, citing the welfare of the affected workers.
“Workers have rights to job security, livelihood and immediate support in the event of company closure,” Federation of Free Workers president Sonny Matula said in a statement on Friday.
“If the primary concern for the raid[s] is the presence of undocumented workers, officials of the Department of Labor and Employment must be part of the government operations,” he added.
Matula’s statement came after an inter-agency law enforcement operation led by the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) that shut down a steel manufacturing plant last August 14.
The factory was allegedly producing substandard and radioactive reinforcing steel bars in Davao City.
Authorities “rescued” 174 workers at the plant, according to the Presidential Anti-Organized Crime Commission (PAOCC).
Matula also pointed to a Kilusang Mayo Uno (KMU) Southern Mindanao statement last August, expressing solidarity with the workers displaced by the raid.
“We… demand immediate assistance, protection of their rights, and accountability from the agencies responsible for the operation and its aftermath,” Matula quoted the KMU statement.
The PAOCC and the NBI previously committed to coordinate with the DOLE in protecting the affected workers. /apl

articles.title: Napolcom to rule soon on cop linked to Tacloban school shooting
articles.summary: TACLOBAN CITY — The National Police Commission (Napolcom) in Eastern Visayas has completed its administrative proceedings against a police officer whose service firearm was allegedly used in the June…

blocks.text: TACLOBAN CITY — The National Police Commission (Napolcom) in Eastern Visayas has completed its administrative proceedings against a police officer whose service firearm was allegedly used in the June 22 shooting at San Jose National High School here and forwarded its findings and recommendations to its central office for a final decision.

Napolcom Eastern Visayas Regional Director Lawyer Risty Sibay said the regional office completed the summary hearing involving Police Staff Sergeant Arla Ray Pacencia and submitted the results to the Napolcom en banc.

“Our office has already undertaken the summary hearing of the said police officer, and we have already submitted the result to our central office en banc for the decision of the administrative case pertaining to the said incident,” Sibay told the Inquirer in an interview on Thursday, Sept. 3.
Sibay declined to disclose the regional office’s findings and recommendations, saying the central office is now considering them. The Napolcom en banc could issue its decision as early as next month.

Pacencia, an active member of the Philippine National Police in Eastern Visayas, is the aunt of the 14-year-old boy identified as one of two suspects in the shooting. She is currently in the custody of the PNP-8 holding unit while the administrative case is pending.

The Department of Justice earlier said a reckless imprudence charge was filed against Pacencia in connection with the incident. Authorities said the service firearm issued to her was allegedly used by the 14-year-old in the attack.

The June 22 shooting at San Jose National High School in Tacloban City left three students dead and 20 others injured, making it one of the most serious school-based shooting incidents reported in the country in recent years.

The incident prompted investigations into not only the attack itself but also how the firearm allegedly used in the shooting was obtained and whether proper safeguards were observed in securing an issued police weapon.

The administrative case before Napolcom is separate from the criminal proceedings arising from the shooting. Napolcom has administrative disciplinary authority over members of the police organization in cases within its jurisdiction, while criminal charges are handled through the regular justice system.
The two minors identified in the case are being handled under the country’s juvenile justice system.

The 14-year-old suspect is exempt from criminal liability because of his age, although authorities may still impose appropriate intervention and rehabilitation measures under the juvenile justice law.
The 15-year-old companion, meanwhile, was earlier charged with three counts of murder, three counts of frustrated murder and multiple counts of serious physical injuries.

Justice Undersecretary Ian Norman Dato said Thursday that Tacloban City prosecutors had also ordered the filing of frustrated murder and attempted murder charges against the 15-year-old, who authorities determined had acted with discernment when he brought a gun to the school and opened fire.

These new filings are in addition to five cases—three counts of murder and two counts of attempted murder—that were earlier filed against him on July 13 before the family court of the Tacloban Regional Trial Court.
Both minors remain in the custody of a rehabilitation facility managed by the Department of Social Welfare and Development.

The parents of the three slain students in previous interviews said they are also calling for the government to file similar charges against the 15-year-old, as the 14-year-old was identified based on witness accounts as the one who shot and killed their children./coa

articles.title: Prosecution drops Lachica, Nolasco, Madriaga as witnesses
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — The prosecution panel in Vice President Sara Duterte’s impeachment trial would no longer call three who were expected to provide key testimony on the alleged misuse of…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The prosecution panel in Vice President Sara Duterte’s impeachment trial would no longer call three who were expected to provide key testimony on the alleged misuse of confidential funds, saying it has established a strong case already.

In an online press briefing on Friday, prosecution spokesperson and advisor Robert Ace Barbers said that former Vice Presidential Security and Protection Group (VPSPG) officials Col. Raymund Dante Lachica and Col. Dennis Nolasco, as well as former Duterte aide Ramil Madriaga, would no longer summoned to testify, as the prosecution believes it has already met the three requirements under Article I of the Articles of Impeachment.

Article I deals with the alleged misuse of confidential funds (CF) lodged within Duterte’s offices, P500 million with the Office of the Vice President (OVP) from 2022 to 2023, and P112.5 million with the Department of Education for the first three quarters of 2023.

“Hindi naman na necessary ‘yong statement ni Col. Lachica dahil nga all the previous witnesses na iniharap ng prosecution at ‘yong mga ebidensyang pinakita sa impeachment court already substantiates ‘yong ating allegations dito sa Article I — ‘yong misuse, ginamit sa mga bagay na hindi in accordance with the Joint Circular,” Barbers told reporters.

(The statements of Col. Lachica are no longer necessary because all the previous witnesses presented by the prosecution and the evidence shown by the impeachment court already substantiates our allegations here in Article I — the misuse, that these funds were used for matters not in accordance with the Joint Circular.)
He said the prosecution panel believes it has established a strong case, although the final assessment rests with the senator-judges.
“Nasa kamay na po ng ating mga Senators-judges kung ano ang kanilang titingan na mas matimbang dito sa mga iniharap natin,” he added.
(It is now in the hands of our senator-judges how they will appreciate the evidence and testimonies we have presented.)

Lachica, former head of the VPSPG, was identified as the person who received the P500 million OVP CF from former special disbursing officer (SDO) Gina Acosta — who earlier testified that it was Duterte who ordered her to transfer the amount to the military official.

Acosta also admitted during the trial that she handed OVP’s CFs to Lachica even if she knew that the latter was not a bonded official — or someone who has issued a bond, in accordance with Item No. 6.1.2 of the Joint Circular No. 2015-01 of the Commission on Audit (COA) and other government offices using CFs.

Under the circular, cash advances for confidential and intelligence funds must be drawn by duly designated and bonded SDOs or the head of agency for programs, activities and projects chargeable to such funds.
Barbers argued that Lachica’s status as a security official and not an OVP employee further supports the prosecution’s allegations involving the release of the funds.
Nolasco was also linked to the handling of confidential funds from the DepEd.
Former Education Undersecretary Michael Poa who previously testified that former DepEd SDO Edward Fajarda released confidential funds to Nolasco upon Duterte’s orders.

Fajarda’s possible appearance before the impeachment court remains uncertain because of his health condition. He had previously told a House committee in 2024 that he transferred the confidential funds to Nolasco.
These statements and the fact that neither Lachica nor Nolasco are OVP and DepEd employees already show violations in the use and liquidation of CFs within Duterte’s office, Barbers claimed.

“At sabi niya (Acosta), upon the orders of the Vice President ibinigay niya ‘yong pera kay Col Lachica who is not even an employee of the Office of the Vice President and is not in charge of disbursing all these funds kasi ang trabaho ni Col. Lachica, bantayan ang ating Pangalawang Pangulo, i-secure siya, ‘yon lamang ang kanyang role ‘di ba?” Barbers said.

(And she (Acosta) said, she gave the funds to Col. Lachica upon the orders of the Vice President, even if he is not an employee of the Office of the Vice President and is not in charge of disbursing all these funds, because Col. Lachica’s actual job is to secure the Vice President, that’s his role, right?)

As for Madriaga, Barbers said the former’s statements during the House committee on justice hearing last April, regarding the two impeachment complaints against Duterte, delivered one of the highlights as it was the first time that any person provided a possible glimpse into how the CFs were allegedly misused and transferred.

Madriaga claimed during the April 14 hearing that Duterte ordered him in December 2022 to coordinate with Col. Dennis Nolasco, regarding the deliveries of cash to allies in San Pablo, Laguna; a comedy bar in Quezon City, and the Office of the Ombudsman parking lot as a way of “returning a favor.”

According to Madriaga, four large duffle bags were unloaded from the vehicles, three of them were dark and one was light-colored — containing around P30 million to P35 million each — corresponding to the P125 million CF issued to OVP in December 2022.
Madriaga claimed that he liquidated the P125 million CF in one day, and not the reported 11 days.
Some details in Madriaga’s account were later echoed by witnesses presented before the impeachment court.
Acosta testified that four oblong-shaped traveling bags were used to carry the OVP’s P125 million confidential fund from a LandBank branch in Shaw Boulevard. /dp

articles.title: Palace: Davao City received P52.8-B nat'l tax allotment from 2022 to 2026
articles.summary: Malacañang said Friday the total national tax allotment (NTA) for Davao City and its barangays from 2022 to 2026 has reached P52.80 billion.

blocks.text: Published September 4, 2026 2:28pm
Malacañang said Friday the total national tax allotment (NTA) for Davao City and its barangays from 2022 to 2026 has reached P52.80 billion.

Palace Press Officer Undersecretary Atty. Claire Castro said that out of this amount, P41.63 billion was the NTA for the Davao City government alone, while the combined NTA of the city's barangays amounted to P11.17 billion.

"Sa sinasabing walang government funding na nilaan sa Davao City, ayon kay Cong. Pulong [Duterte], ito ang totoo," the Palace official said, referring to Davao City Representative Paolo Duterte, the brother of Vice President Sara Duterte.
(Regarding the claim of Cong. Pulong [Duterte] that no government funding was allocated to Davao City, this is the truth.)

Aside from the NTA, Castro said Davao City also received various funding releases of approximately P314.48 million under the General Appropriations Act (GAA) for fiscal years 2022 to 2026. These include:

items: P4.92 million — Special Shares in the Proceeds of National Taxes - Share in the Utilization and Development of National Wealth
P25.14 million — Special Shares in the Proceeds of National Taxes - Share in Incremental Collections from Value Added Tax
P175.50 million — Local Government Support Fund - Financial Assistance to Local Government Units
P18.61 million — Local Government Support Fund - Support to the Barangay Development Program of the National Task Force to End Local Communist Armed Conflict
P10.65 million — Local Government Support Fund - Support and Assistance Fund to Participatory Budgeting
P79.55 million — Special Shares of Local Government Units in the Proceeds of Fire Code Fees

blocks.text: "Kung pagsasamahin ang P52.80 billion na NTA at ang P314.48 million na iba pang releases na nakasaad sa attachment, aabot sa humigit-kumulang P53.11 billion ang kabuuang pondong nakatala para sa Davao City at mga barangay nito mula FY 2022 hanggang FY 2026," Castro said.

(If the P52.80 billion NTA and the P314.48 million in other releases are combined, the total funds allocated for Davao City and its barangays from FY 2022 to FY 2026 reach approximately P53.11 billion.)

She noted that this amount does not yet include the individual programs and projects of government agencies for Davao City, such as the Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD), Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH), Department of Transportation (DOTr), and Department of Agriculture (DA).
GMA News Online reached out to Congressman Duterte for a comment, but he has yet to respond as of posting time.

Under the Constitution and the Local Government Code, the NTA represents the automatic and formula-based share of local government units (LGUs) in national internal revenue, serving as a primary source of funding for local programs, projects, and services.
The NTA for fiscal year 2026, amounting to P1.19 trillion, was fully released by the Department of Budget and Management (DBM) in January.
This was directly credited to the authorized government servicing banks of LGUs, in accordance with existing budgeting, accounting, and auditing rules. — VDV, GMA News

articles.title: Charles Perrottet denies asking brother as premier to appoint cabinet minister, Icac hears
articles.summary: Charles says claims by developer Jean Nassif in an intercepted phone call that ‘we’re reshuffling the government’ did not reflect promises allegedly made to Nassif

blocks.text: The younger brother of Dominic Perrottet has denied asking his brother to appoint a cabinet minister to achieve outcomes for a property developer, a corruption inquiry has heard.

Charles Perrottet told the Independent Commission Against Corruption (Icac) on Friday that claims made in an intercepted phone call featuring developer Jean Nassif days before his brother became the NSW premier – in which Nassif described Dominic Perrottet as “my boy” – did not reflect promises allegedly made to Nassif.
Dominic Perrottet is not a person of interest in Icac’s inquiry and is not accused of any wrongdoing.

As part of its inquiry into alleged corruption in the NSW Liberals, Icac is investigating the allegation that conservative factional figures Charles Perrottet, Jeremy Greenwood and Christian Ellis received prohibited donations totalling $2m from Nassif or his company Toplace between 2020 and 2023 in exchange for political outcomes.

Those outcomes allegedly included damage to the career of David Elliott, a former NSW Liberal minister, who had opposed Nassif’s developments and the removal of the former building commissioner David Chandler, who was scrutinising defects in Toplace apartments.

On Friday, the commission heard a phone call featuring Nassif, lawfully intercepted by police, made on 2 October 2021. Three days later, Dominic Perrottet was chosen as premier by Liberal MPs, defeating Rob Stokes, under a deal Charles Perrottet helped broker between conservative and moderate factions.
In the call, Nassif allegedly told a relative: “This week is going to be the worst week of my life … because we’re reshuffling the government.”

“We thought we [had] done it, then this wanker the police minister he did it, and he had a caucus, and he convinced Rob Stokes to challenge my boy,” Nassif continued, saying he supported Perrottet’s campaign. “They’re my people, they’re the right wing”.
Nassif told the relative he had been promised that then police minister Elliott and the then fair trading minister Kevin Anderson would be removed.
“I put my lady in in his position [sic], the consumer affairs minister … then I’m gonna … have to step on fucking David Chandler and get rid of him.”

The former NSW fair trading minister Eleni Petinos has previously told the inquiry she may have been used by fellow Liberals, including Chris Spence and Charles Perrotet, to get rid of Chandler, including attempts to persuade her Chandler was “dodgy”. She is not named in Icac’s allegations and is not accused of any wrongdoing.

On Friday, Charles Perrottet told counsel assisting, Peggy Dwyer SC, that following his brother’s accession as premier, he did not discuss the makeup of his cabinet with him. He later said he did recall “a conversation about the balance of women in the cabinet”, which he said he did not include names.

He said he did not discuss Petinos, or put her forward for the fair trading portfolio. “Dom would have made his own decisions,” he said. He said he did not recall having a conversation with Nassif about Petinos.

In another intercepted phone call to an unnamed person in January 2022, after Elliott had been moved to transport in a reshuffle the previous month, Nassif claimed he had “stripped him from his police ministry”.
“I’m gonna fuck everyone. The commissioner, [in] a couple of weeks he’ll be gone.”
Charles Perrottet, acknowledging that “commissioner” probably referred to Chandler, said: “You can’t take this seriously.”

Chandler resigned in July 2022 citing concerns with Petinos, who was sacked in that month amid bullying allegations which she denied at the time. Chandler, who was later persuaded to reverse his resignation, is not a person of interest in Icac’s allegations and is not accused of any wrongdoing.

The inquiry has previously heard that following a meeting between him and Nassif at the fine-dining Nobu restaurant in Melbourne in May 2021, Charles Perrottet wrote he had told Nassif “the best way to get the building commissioner off his back is to take the fight to Elliott and dismantle his infrastructure”. In another message he asked for payments in relation to Toplace developments.
Charles Perrottet, asked if Nassif’s claims were consistent with promises made at the dinner, said on Friday: “I wouldn’t put it that way”.

He has repeatedly denied taking payments from Nassif for political outcomes, saying he would regularly lie to the developer, adding a “political flavour” to advice in order to chase payments for genuine lobbying work by Beckington, a firm controlled by Greenwood and Ellis.
Nassif, who fled Australia for rural Lebanon in 2022, withdrew from an expected appearance by video link on Friday after providing a medical certificate. He has previously denied any wrongdoing.
Greenwood will appear before the commission again next week.
Icac’s inquiry continues.

articles.title: Australian ski resorts to close up to a month early due to global heating and El Niño
articles.summary: ‘Challenging’ weather conditions and lack of snowfall are being blamed after a winter that broke multiple heat records
articles.byline: Graham Readfearn Environment and climate correspondent

blocks.text: Major Australian alpine resorts are closing their ski operations up to a month early after a winter that broke multiple records for heat with limited snow falls being washed away by rain.

Predictions in June that a building El Niño could combine with global heating for a challenging ski season came to pass, with seven resorts either already closed or announcing ski lifts will stop operating this weekend.
This week the Victorian resorts of Mount Buller, Mount Hotham and Falls Creek, together with Charlotte Pass in New South Wales, all announced ski operations would end this weekend.
The Victorian resort of Mount Baw Baw, the NSW resort at Selwyn and Tasmania’s Ben Lomond have already closed. Resorts typically aim to stay open until the first weekend of October.
Resorts blamed “challenging” weather conditions and lack of snowfall. Two other major NSW resorts at Perisher and Thredbo remain open.

“The season was frankly a shocker. This was the fourth disappointing season since 2020,” said Dr Andrew Watkins, a climate scientist and adjunct professor at the Monash University and a science adviser to the campaign group Protect our Winters.
“The problems were El Niño and climate change. It was not that dry this year, but the problem was the warmth. The heat just did us in.”
Watkins, who is also a keen skier, said winter temperatures had been too high and precipitation that might have fallen as snow, had instead fallen as rain.
“Rain is the natural enemy of a snowpack. It melts it and then washes it away,” he said.

Data from the Bureau of Meteorology show Falls Creek and Mount Hotham had their wettest winters in more than 30 years but, together with Mount Buller, they also had their warmest winters on record for average maximum and minimum temperatures.
Watkins said data from weather observations at Cabramurra in Kosciuszko national park suggested alpine winters had warmed by about 2C since the 1960s.
He said that temperature rise would have been the difference between precipitation falling as rain instead of snow. “It would have been a bumper season if it had been 50 years ago,” he said.
The El Niño currently in place in the Pacific Ocean can promote hotter and drier temperatures in Australia’s south-east in winter and spring.
This week the bureau forecast the current El Niño would be the strongest on record and Australian scientists said climate change had made the strength of the event six times more likely.
after newsletter promotion

A bureau spokesperson said this winter’s heat was consistent “with a developing strong El Niño” and the season had seen long periods of high pressure in the Tasman Sea that directed warmer air from the north over alpine regions.
“But winter 2026 also experienced relatively warm nights, with cloud cover and moist soils resulting in less overnight cooling,” the spokesperson said.

“This is in contrast with historical El Niño events. This is all occurring against the background of a globally warmer climate, with daily global surface air temperatures since June close to or above the record levels in 2024.”
New South Wales, Tasmania and Victoria all recorded their hottest winters on record this year.
In July, many ski resorts broke all-time heat records for the month with temperatures during one hot spell up to 12C above average.
Climate scientists have been warning for decades that global heating will create a challenging future for Australia’s ski resorts and alpine habitats.
Josh Elliott, chief executive at the representative body Snow Resorts Australia, said there was “no question it has been a challenging season for natural snowfall”.

“This winter was shaped by a combination of abnormally warm weather and climatic variability, but it’s important to remember that in any outdoor environment, that variability can result in some seasons being better than others.
“This is an abnormal season and shouldn’t be considered in isolation as a reflection of what future seasons will look like.”

He said skiing, snowboarding and snow play had still been available in NSW, Victoria and the ACT “since the June long weekend, with all resorts across Australia operating through the July school holidays and beyond”.
“What this season has shown is the importance and value of the investment resorts have made in snow making, with underlying demand for snow holidays remaining strong through July and August.”

articles.title: DOH accused anew of buying near-expiry drugs for kickbacks
articles.summary: Sen. Raffy Tulfo has accused the Department of Health of deliberately buying up medicine close to its expiration date from favored suppliers to open up an avenue for "kickbacks" using the cheaper…

blocks.text: September 4, 2026 | 2:08pm

MANILA, Philippines — Sen. Raffy Tulfo has accused the Department of Health of deliberately buying up medicine close to its expiration date from favored suppliers to open up an avenue for "kickbacks" using the cheaper drugs.

During Friday's (September 4) Senate deliberations of the DOH's proposed 2027 budget, Tulfo confronted newly appointed Health Secretary Edwin Mercado over the possible scheme that has also led to the expiration of billions of pesos worth of medicine in government warehouses.
The senator said in 2023, at least P11 billion worth of expired drugs were "buried underground (ibinaon sa lupa)."
"Dapat diyan may makulong. Dapat diyan may mapugutan ng ulo eh. Napaka-eskandalo ng amount na 'yan," he said.
(Someone should be arrested. Someone's head should roll. That amount is scandalous).

Tulfo first called out the DOH over whether it can "guarantee" the public that the medicines it procures for 2027 would not expire before use, before asking if it is a ploy to get near-expired medicine in the procurement process.
"Ayon sa aking source, sinasadyang bibilhin about to be expired kasi mas mura at galing sa mga pinapaboran na mga supplier," he added.
(Based on my source, it's intentionally purchased when it is about to be expired, because it is cheaper and sourced from favored suppliers.)
"Just imagine how many millions of kickbacks in the past years for the procurement officer," Tulfo said in mixed English and Filipino.
Mercado, who assumed his post as DOH chief on August 10, confirmed that one of the DOH undersecretaries who recently stepped down handled procurement.
Randy Escolango, the former DOH undersecretary for financial and supply chain management services, resigned on August 15 while facing a complaint before the Office of the Ombudsman.
DOH employees filed a complaint in June accusing former Health Secretary Ted Herbosa and Escolango of a "self-policing conflict of interest."

The filing alleges Escolango had unchecked authority over drug procurement by serving as Bids and Awards Committee chair while simultaneously managing the department's finance and supply chain functions. Escolango has not publicly addressed the allegations.

State auditors have found expired or expiring DOH medicine worth P18.5 billion from 2015 to 2018, P2.2 billion in 2019, P95.15 million in 2020, P85 million in 2021, P7.4 billion in 2022, and P11.18 billion in 2023 — the last figure including more than 7 million vials of expired COVID-19 vaccines and 24,539 bags of donated dialysis solution. In 2024, Commission on Audit found P34.8 million of drugs already expired, with a further P99.5 million nearing expiration.
COA has flagged the DOH for gaps in procurement planning, poor distribution, and weak monitoring of its inventory.
18-month shelf life rule?

Responding more broadly to questions about how the DOH could guarantee that newly procured drugs would not be near their expiration date, Meraco pointed to the 18-month shelf-life rule and the disqualification of non-compliant suppliers as existing safeguards.

"Napakahigpit na po ngayon doon sa procurement na dapat po talaga 18 months po yung stocks na darating (We're very strict now with the requirement that the stocks have an 18-month shelf life)," Mercado said.

Tulfo however raised the possibility that something is amiss with the timing of purchases. He claimed the department gets around the 18-month rule by delaying the purchase of medicine it knows it needs until shortages become declared emergencies, which then allows it to bypass competitive bidding.
"'Yun 'yung modus diyan sa DOH (That is the modus at the DOH)," he said.
Mercado told the committee the department was pursuing three changes to avoid its stock of drugs from expiring in warehouses.

First, he said the department would channel more of its medicine procurement budget through the Philippine Health Insurance Corp. (PhilHealth), which he said could negotiate bulk, discounted prices directly with suppliers using its own pharmacists.

The second change, Mercado said, is already being enforced: with only 40% of medicine procured centrally by DOH, the remaining 60% — mostly common medicines available locally — are bought through the department's regional Centers for Health Development.
Mercado said the department was also overhauling its inventory-tracking IT system.
"But as what Sen. Tulfo said, I will be creating an investigating committee," Mercado said.
Tulfo pointed out that a similar body — the department's own Inter-Office Task Force — already existed.

However, a member of the task force present during the hearing, Undersecretary Gloria Balboa, said they do not investigate medicine wastage and instead hold weekly meetings on policy, procurement and supply chain issues.
Possible Blue Ribbon probe
Tulfo said a full Senate Blue Ribbon probe may be called soon into the hoarding and drug wastage at the department.

In the same hearing, Tulfo lamented how mental health drugs accounted for the bulk of DOH’s 2026 waste—including stock meant for the Mandaluyong Mental Health Center that expired because staff lacked training to administer it.
He also cited tip-offs that expired inventory was fraudulently relabeled and resold outside official channels.
"You in DOH don't have the capability to administer this, so it just expired," Tulfo said.

Tulfo further questioned why the department had to spend P3 billion to replenish TB medicine stocks after a previous P3.225-billion procurement was suspended in July by former Health Secretary Jose "Brix" Pujalte Jr.
Pujalte, who resigned in August amid the conflict-of-interest allegations and a reported casino scandal, claimed the pause was for inventory verification.
Mercado confirmed the stalled purchase has since resumed.
The Philippines ranks third globally in tuberculosis burden, according to the World Health Organization.
Tulfo urged Mercado to overhaul the DOH's inventory system and stop the massive drug expiration.

"Build a system. Hopefully, you can perfect it so no medicines expire," Tulfo said. "If expiration is unavoidable, it shouldn't reach P100 million. P1 million or P2 million is tolerable—but hundreds of millions... Meanwhile, many health centers aren't getting medicines."
The DOH has a proposed P353.8 billion for 2027 under the National Expenditure Program, P95 billion or 21% lower than its enacted budget this year of P448 billion.

articles.title: First BARMM elections set for Sept. 14 after four postponements
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — After four postponements, the first parliamentary elections in the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM) will be held on Sept. 14. President Ferdinand Marcos…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — After four postponements, the first parliamentary elections in the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM) will be held on Sept. 14.
President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. said last month that the elections are crucial to the development of the region, which he described as a product of a decades-long peace process that began in 1968.

For Marcos, the participation of former secessionists in the elections, including through campaigning, shows they have chosen the political process over armed struggle to pursue peace and progress in the region.

Under the Bangsamoro Organic Law, or Republic Act (RA) No. 11054, which established the BARMM in 2019, the first parliamentary elections were initially scheduled for May 2022, when the mandate of the Bangsamoro Transition Authority (BTA) was expected to end.
The elections were later moved to May 2025, then to Oct. 13 of the same year under RA No. 12123. RA No. 12317 eventually set the elections for the second Monday of September.

Under the Bangsamoro Organic Law, signed by then-President Rodrigo Duterte, voters in the region will elect 80 members of Parliament: 40 party representatives, 32 district representatives and eight sectoral representatives.
The sectoral seats are reserved for women, youth, traditional leaders, ulama or Islamic scholars, settler communities and other sectors.
RELATED STORY: Zubiri launches book on Bangsamoro Organic Law creation

Sen. Juan Miguel Zubiri, the principal author of the law that created the BARMM, earlier said the latest postponement was necessary to give the region more time for institution-building, address governance limitations and ensure a smoother transition.
New districting law

In January, the BTA passed Parliament Bill No. 415, a measure providing for the apportionment of parliamentary district representative seats in the BARMM, clearing the final legal requirement for the region to proceed with its first parliamentary elections.

Last year, the BTA failed to pass the redistricting bill despite an earlier commitment to do so by Dec. 31. The measure was needed to comply with a Supreme Court decision that, without an approved districting framework, the Commission on Elections (Comelec) could not proceed with election preparations.

The measure established the 32 parliamentary districts of the BARMM. It was approved on third and final reading before dawn on Jan. 13, following a special session that began on Jan. 12. The measure received 48 votes in favor, 19 against and four abstentions.
Two weeks later, Comelec postponed the March 30, 2026, Bangsamoro Parliamentary Election.
“Legally and operationally, we can no longer hold the BPE on March 30,” Comelec Chairman George Garcia said. “Operationally, we can no longer afford the one month and two weeks to hold the BPE.”
Marcos eventually signed into law the bill resetting the first regular elections in the BARMM to the second Monday of September, which falls on Sept. 14 this year.

RA No. 12317 states that “to synchronize the BARMM parliamentary elections with the national and local polls, the regular elections for the Bangsamoro Government shall be held on the second Monday of May 2031 and every three years thereafter.”
Significant step

The Office of the Presidential Adviser on Peace, Reconciliation, and Unity commended the BTA for passing the new districting law, congratulating its members for heeding the call of the Bangsamoro people to hold the region’s first regular parliamentary elections.

“The passage of Parliament Bill No. 415 in a special session on January 12 is seen as a major step by the BTA towards establishing a fully functioning, representative, and democratic government in the Bangsamoro, anchored on the provisions of the Comprehensive Agreement on the Bangsamoro (CAB),” it said.

Then-Presidential Peace Adviser Carlito G. Galvez Jr. said the approval of a legally compliant redistricting law reflected the BTA’s resolve to uphold democratic principles, ensure inclusive representation and realize the aspirations of Bangsamoro communities for self-governance.

“The law’s passage aligns with the peace, reconciliation and unity agenda of the Marcos administration, and its commitment to uphold its deliverables under all signed Bangsamoro peace agreements,” he said.
Government never lost hope

Despite the postponements, Marcos said that “the government never lost hope and remains fully committed to supporting this democratic exercise,” adding that “we are prepared for the first parliamentary elections in the BARMM.”
He made the statement during the opening ceremony of the 2026 National Peace Consciousness Month at the Ceremonial Hall of Malacañan Palace.

The monthlong observance commemorates the 30th anniversary of the signing of the 1996 Final Peace Agreement with the Moro National Liberation Front, the 40th anniversary of the 1986 Mount Data Peace Accord and the signing of the Agreement on the Fulfillment of the Mount Data Peace Accord with the Cordillera Bodong Administration-Cordillera People’s Liberation Army.

“Be assured that this Administration will do everything within our mandate to ensure that the elections are safe, peaceful, and credible. We will protect the right of every Bangsamoro voter to cast a ballot freely and without fear,” Marcos said.
He urged BARMM voters to show that the region’s future is shaped by their voices, choices and hopes for their communities.

Officials elected in the BARMM parliamentary elections will serve from noon on Oct. 30, 2026, to June 30, 2031. Beginning in 2031, elected officials will assume office at noon on June 30 following their election. /dm — with reports from Luisa Cabato

articles.title: Bonoan faces arraignment in remaining flood control graft case
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Former Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) chief Manuel Bonoan appeared Friday before the Sandiganbayan Second Division for the arraignment on his remaining graft…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Former Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) chief Manuel Bonoan appeared Friday before the Sandiganbayan Second Division for the arraignment on his remaining graft case over his alleged involvement in a kickback scheme related to flood control projects.
The Office of the Ombudsman accepted his offer to become a state witness, prompting the anti-graft body to drop the charges against him.
Earlier, Bonoan was released from hospital arrest at the Philippine National Police General Hospital in Camp Crame after his plunder case before the Sandiganbayan Fifth Division was dropped.

His plunder case kept Bonoan behind bars, so Ombudsman prosecutors filed before the Fifth Division a motion to amend the information so he could be removed from the charges. On Tuesday, the division granted this motion.
Only Sen. Jinggoy Estrada and three other former DPWH officials remain as accused in the plunder case.
However, the anti-graft court Second Division denied the prosecutors motion to amend information to discharge Bonoan, this time from the graft charge.

Bonoan’s graft case stemmed from his alleged conspiracy with Estrada to ensure the inclusion of flood control projects in Bulacan in the 2025 budget where the senator allegedly got a P213.7 million kickback.
For his part, Estrada did not enter a plea during his arraignment, prompting the Second Division to enter a not guilty plea on his behalf.
Prosecutors on August 10 filed a motion for reconsideration (MR) on the Second Division’s denial of their motion to amend the information to discharge Bonoan.
This MR is expected to be tackled during the arraignment proceeding. /jpv

articles.title: Marcos signs law putting poorest students first in college subsidies
articles.summary: After poorest students lost share of college aid, a new law aims to put them first.

blocks.text: September 4, 2026 | 1:15pm
Students return to their respective schools as in-person classes in Marikina City resume on March 9, 2023.

MANILA, Philippines — President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. signed a new law Friday, September 4, that gives the most economically disadvantaged college and vocational students first priority for government subsidies, after past data shows aid has increasingly gone to wealthier applicants instead.

The new law, Republic Act 12325, introduces amendments to the Universal Access to Quality Tertiary Education Act (Republic Act 10931) that allocates more slots in financial assistance programs for college students from the poorest households.

Specifically, it sets up a prioritization system for eligible students in the Commission on Higher Education's Tertiary Education Subsidy (TES), where students from households enrolled in the Pantawid Pamilyang Pilipino Program get the highest priority, while remaining slots go to applicants based on household income.

The Second Congressional Commission on Education (EDCOM 2), which pushed for the amendments, previously found that the poorest households' share of TES grants fell from 74.24% in 2018 to 30.74% in 2022, even though the subsidy was meant to prioritize them.

"The amendments ensure that government assistance reaches those who need it most, particularly students from poor and disadvantaged families, including qualified 4Ps beneficiaries," Marcos said at the signing in Malacañang.

The law also creates a new program, Private Education Assistance, or PEA, to help poor students taking priority courses — but not covered by other grants — attend CHED-recognized private colleges and TESDA-registered technical schools.

Under the law, subsidy amounts given will now vary by degree program instead of a flat rate — currently P27,000 a year per semester for private colleges and P20,000 for public — which EDCOM 2 said had limited students to choosing from a narrow set of programs, including business administration, education and information technology. Students taking government-priority courses will get extra funding on top of that.
The subsidy will also cover internship and clinical training fees for nursing and other health-related programs, costs students previously had to pay themselves.

Marcos ordered the Commission on Higher Education, the Technical Education and Skills Development Authority, and the Unified Student Financial Assistance System for Tertiary Education to draft the law's implementing rules.

The law was authored by Reps. Roman Romulo (Pasig) and Jude Acidre (TINGOG party-list) and Sens. Bam Aquino, Joel Villanueva and Loren Legarda. It was on the executive's priority list for the 20th Congress.
The TES is only one of four components of the original RA 10931, the law that was passed in 2017 that made tuition in government-run colleges and universities free.

Under TES, students enrolled in state universities and colleges receive additional financial assistance, such as allowances for books, instructional materials, transportation, board and lodging, and daily living expenses.

While tuition and mandatory fees are already covered under the law's free tuition provision, the TES provides allowance grants to financially needy students to offset the indirect costs of pursuing a degree.

The other two components of the law are the Free Technical-Vocational Education and Training, which waives training and assessment fees for state-run technical-vocational iinstitutes; and the Student Loan Program.

articles.title: President Javier Milei says ‘winds of change’ support Argentina’s claim to Falkland Islands
articles.summary:
President cites Donald Trump’s suggestion that he might reconsider US support for British sovereignty, and threatens swifter sanctions on British oil interests

President Javier Milei has…

blocks.text: President Javier Milei has said “winds of change favourable” to Argentina’s claim to the Falkland Islands were “blowing around the world” in a televised address, citing signs that Donald Trump might reconsider the US position on the islands’ sovereignty.
“Recently, President Trump declared that the US is re-evaluating its historic position in relation to the Malvinas,” he said, using the Argentinian name for the islands.

The Argentinian president said the UK was facing “multiple crises of a migratory, demographic and economic nature that are unlikely to be resolved. It is clear that they are on a path of decline. Argentina’s future, however, is flourishing and will prevail.”

Earlier on Thursday, Trump was asked by British outlet GB News if he would “come to the UK’s aid” during a potential territorial dispute over the Falkland Islands with Argentina, and hinted that he would not, adding that the UK “weren’t there to help me [with Iran]”.
Supporters had expected Milei to use his address to the nation on Thursday night to announce an unprecedented US endorsement of Argentina’s sovereignty claim over the Falkland Islands.

Instead, the self-styled libertarian, when asked whether he was reviewing the US position on the islands, repeated the US president’s words, saying: “I always review every position. That’s just one of many.”
The far-right president then portrayed Trump’s response as a “threat” that was “not innocuous”.

“The US is considering this change of position because it knows that Argentina has a reliable partner, aligned with western values, in a strategically important position that can be a valuable ally in the decades to come,” he said.

The US has formally recognised the UK’s de facto administration of the islands but has not taken a formal position on sovereignty. The first reports of a possible revision emerged in April, when an internal Pentagon email reported by Reuters raised the prospect of Washington reconsidering its stance as one possible way of punishing Nato allies that declined to join the Iran war.

In Thursday’s interview, Trump said of the UK: “Your country was not there to help me. We didn’t need help, but I did ask Nato, and I asked your former leader [Keir Starmer], ‘why don’t you send a couple of ships?’. He said, ‘We don’t have any’. It was pretty sad, the whole thing.”

Despite the expectations created by Milei and his supporters – the president summoned all his ministers to stand alongside him – the main new elements of the speech were a few decrees announced by the president.

One of them is to speed up sanctions “against those participating in oil extraction initiatives”, specifically citing an offshore oil project in the North Falkland Basin led by the Israeli company Navitas alongside its British partner Rockhopper. Milei claimed the project violated a UN call for neither Argentina nor the UK to take unilateral action in the territory.

Despite his “radical” austerity policies, Milei also said he would sign an emergency decree to increase resources for the defence ministry, prioritising the construction of an integrated naval base in Tierra del Fuego. The project to build a base there predates Milei, and construction began in 2022.

The UK said earlier this week that its position on the Falklands was “long-standing and unwavering”. It said in a statement: “Sovereignty rests with the UK, and the islanders’ right to self-determination is paramount. The UK’s position is clear. The islanders have repeatedly expressed their wish to remain a British overseas territory.”

Some analysts had already viewed Milei’s recent embrace of the Malvinas cause as another attempt to create a “smokescreen” at the lowest point of his popularity since taking office. He is expected to seek re-election next year.

Amid corruption allegations involving members of his government and poor economic results – his “chainsaw” austerity policies have brought inflation under control, but unemployment and poverty have risen – the far-right president has increasingly turned up the volume on controversial measures, including claims of an anti-Argentina campaign dating back to the World Cup, attacks on Brazil’s leftwing president, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, and an immigration crackdown modelled on the US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE).

Many have also noted that his interest in the issue is recent. Milei had long described himself as a great admirer of Margaret Thatcher, the British prime minister during the 1982 Falklands war, and only began adopting a public pro-sovereignty stance a few months ago, after reports emerged that the US might be reconsidering its position.
The far-right leader also dismissed the principle of self-determination invoked by the UK – in a 2013 referendum, 99.8% of the islanders voted to remain a British overseas territory.
Echoing the same phrase used by Argentina’s national team on a banner celebrating their victory over England in the World Cup semi-final, Milei said that “The Malvinas are Argentinian.”

In its 10:30 a.m. monitoring report, the PDRRMO said none of the province’s five congressional districts reported affected individuals.

articles.title: Tulfo grills new FDA officer-in-charge over alleged ties to ex-chief
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Sen. Raffy Tulfo on Friday grilled newly appointed Food and Drug Administration (FDA) Officer-in-Charge (OIC) Franklin Anthony Tabaquin IV, alleging that he was appointed to the…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Sen. Raffy Tulfo on Friday grilled newly appointed Food and Drug Administration (FDA) Officer-in-Charge (OIC) Franklin Anthony Tabaquin IV, alleging that he was appointed to the position because of his ties to former FDA chief Paolo Teston.
During the Senate Committee on Finance’s hearing on the Department of Health’s (DOH) spending plan for 2027, Tulfo questioned Tabaquin’s appointment.

blocks.caption: Atty. Franklin Anthony Tabaquin IV – Screengrabbed from Senate of the Philippines / YouTube

blocks.text: “Bakit ikaw ang na-appoint? Samantalang marami naman diyan mas qualified pa sa iyo sa FDA, who’s been there for so many years, at alam nila ins and out ng FDA, and yet ikaw in-appoint. Mali. Nagkamali ang Malacañang, kasi bitbit ka ni Teston,” the senator said.

(Why were you appointed? There are many others there who are more qualified than you in the FDA, who have been there for so many years and know the ins and outs of the FDA, and yet you were appointed. That’s wrong. Malacañang made a mistake because Teston brought you along)

Tulfo also revived his longstanding criticism of Teston, whom he accused in 2025 of failing to effectively enforce FDA warnings and challenged to resign over the continued online sale of banned products.
Asked about his appointment again later in the hearing, Tabaquin confirmed that Teston had recruited him.
“Nag-apply po ako. Ako ay nirecruit nga po ako ni Atty. Paolo Teston po,” Tabaquin said.
(I applied for the position. I was recruited by Atty. Paolo Teston)
Tulfo then asked Tabaquin about a case allegedly filed against him before the Office of the Ombudsman.
“Meron kang kaso sa Ombudsman, graft and corruption, pending, tama? Bakit ka kinasuhan sa Ombudsman?” Tulfo asked.
(You have a pending case before the Ombudsman for graft and corruption, correct? Why were you charged before the Ombudsman?)
Tabaquin, for his part, said the allegations involved delays that occurred before he assumed his current positions.
“It’s very unfortunate nga po… In my 15 years of government service po, ngayon lang po ako nakasuhan… At yung mga kaso kasi, mga delays po na nangyari po way, way before my time,” Tabaquin said.
(It’s actually very unfortunate… In my 15 years of government service, this is the first time I’ve been charged… The cases involved allegations of delays that happened way, way before my time)

He said he only became OIC deputy director for operations in October last year, was officially appointed deputy director in July this year, and had been serving as the FDA’s OIC director general for only two weeks.
Tulfo, however, maintained that Tabaquin’s appointment raised concerns because of his association with Teston.

“Nothing personal to what I’m going to say to you. You don’t deserve to be the Director General because marami pang mas magagaling diyan sa iyo. Binitbit ka lang eh ni Teston, dinala ka diyan,” Tulfo said.

(Nothing personal about what I’m going to say to you… You don’t deserve to be the Director General because there are many others there who are more qualified than you. Teston was the one who brought you in and brought you there)
“For me, ikaw ay bata ni Teston. So kung ano mga kalokohan ni Teston, ipagpapatuloy lang ‘yan,” he added, recalling that he had previously challenged Teston to resign and accused him of wrongdoing.
(For me, you are Teston’s protégé. So whatever wrongdoings Teston did, you will just continue them,)
Tulfo said he would bring the matter to the Senate Blue Ribbon Committee for a broader investigation.

During the same budget hearing, Tulfo again questioned the DOH over the continued expiration and disposal of medicines worth hundreds of millions of pesos, demanding records to determine why the drugs were procured and why supposedly near-expiry medicines were accepted.
He likewise reiterated his calls for an investigation into the matter, saying the wastage was particularly alarming amid shortages of medicines in some health centers. /jpv
