Ken earlier said he met Paras and the lawyers in a restaurant in July to supposedly plan the “character assassination” scheme in which four of his female artists would issue fabricated statements claiming that Recto forced them to use illegal drugs and have sex with him.
The lawyers, who allegedly introduced themselves as Leviste’s representatives, were tasked with crafting the “script,” or fabricated statements targeting Recto, the talent manager said.

articles.title: Europe weighs solutions to curtail Russia’s growing hybrid warfare
articles.summary:
Governments now moving faster to impose costs on Moscow for its increasing attacks over support for Ukraine

Russia’s suspected sabotage campaign across Europe appears to be gathering pace…

blocks.text: Russia’s suspected sabotage campaign across Europe appears to be gathering pace again, confronting governments with a problem they have struggled to solve since the start of the war in Ukraine: how to impose a meaningful cost on Moscow for attacks that remain deliberately below the threshold of conventional war.

Over the past month alone, an explosives-laden drone was discovered next to a Ukrainian cargo plane at Germany’s Leipzig airport, Poland has faced suspected acts of sabotage, and a string of unexplained explosions and fires have hit defence facilities supplying Ukraine across Europe.

The attacks, aimed at sowing chaos and undermining support for Ukraine, vary widely in their ambition and sophistication, but share a common feature: they are often difficult to trace conclusively back to Moscow.

That ambiguity is built into the way the operations are organised. Russian intelligence services have shifted away from relying primarily on professional operatives dispatched across Europe. Instead, suspected saboteurs are increasingly recruited remotely, including through Telegram channels, and paid in cryptocurrency to carry out individual tasks – allowing the Russian intelligence officers directing them to remain safely at home.
The pattern was evident in Denmark this week, where authorities warned that Moscow was recruiting Danish citizens to carry out sabotage against defence companies with ties to Ukraine.
But the growing scale of the attacks, and the speed with which European governments are now prepared to point the finger at Moscow, suggest the mood may be changing.

When an incendiary parcel burst into flames at DHL’s Leipzig hub in July 2024, it took about nine months before German investigators reported a concrete link to the GRU, Russia’s military intelligence agency.

blocks.caption: A police officer in protective clothing walks next to an explosive-disarming robot (EOD) at Leipzig airport after a drone was found near a runway last month. Photograph: Axel Schmidt/Reuters

blocks.text: This time, Berlin moved far faster. Within days of the second incident at Leipzig airport, German officials publicly blamed Moscow – a sign both of growing confidence in identifying Russian operations and diminishing patience with what officials see as an increasingly brazen campaign of sabotage.
Yet while Berlin has become quicker to point the finger at Moscow, its punishment for now has followed a more cautious path.

Germany’s response to the failed Leipzig drone attack appeared calibrated to keep tensions in check, underscoring the harder question of what Europe can actually do beyond sanctions and diplomatic expulsions without risking a direct military confrontation.

Berlin announced the closure of a Russian cultural centre and a Russian consulate, prompting Moscow to shut down the already gutted Goethe-Institut – a measured retaliation rather than a real escalation.

Europe’s room for retaliation is also constrained by the powers given to its intelligence agencies. Unlike the CIA, many European services are primarily tasked with collecting intelligence and have far less latitude to conduct covert operations abroad. That leaves governments with relatively few tools between diplomatic and economic punishment on one end of the spectrum and overt military action on the other. To counter the shortcoming, several EU states, including the Netherlands, have recently put forward bills that would greatly expand the surveillance powers of the country’s intelligence agencies

blocks.caption: British armed forces intercept a Russian shadow fleet vessel in the Channel in June. Photograph: LPhot Hutchins/MoD Crown copyright/PA

blocks.text: One area where Europe can point to more tangible action is its growing willingness to detain vessels linked to Russia’s shadow fleet. On Wednesday, Norwegian authorities seized a Russian vessel in the Arctic archipelago of Svalbard at Ukraine’s request.
But critics argue that such measures are still not enough to deter Moscow.
“Every time we do nothing, we invite Putin to continue,” said one EU lawmaker, speaking on condition of anonymity.
That argument has been made most forcefully by Poland and the Baltic states, which have consistently pushed their western European allies to take a harder line against Moscow.

“Hybrid war is not just a nuisance on the internet,” the Polish foreign minister, Radosław Sikorski, said on Thursday. “Hybrid war means assassination squads, it means arsonists, it means blowing up moving trains, like in Poland, it means breaches of airspace with drones and cruise missiles.”
“We need to convince Putin that such actions are not for free,” he added.

At the same time, Sikorski also appeared to acknowledge, somewhat jokingly, the limits of Europe’s existing toolkit. Recalling Poland’s response to previous suspected Russian operations, he said: “Every time Russia committed arson or tried to blow up a moving train … I closed one Russian consulate, but I ran out of consulates to close.”
Jakub Krupa contributed reporting

articles.title: Chinese man, 2 others nabbed in alleged P300,000 cellphone robbery
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — A Chinese man and two of his alleged cohorts were arrested in Makati City for allegedly attempting to rob two individuals during a deal to purchase P300,000 worth of cellphones,…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — A Chinese man and two of his alleged cohorts were arrested in Makati City for allegedly attempting to rob two individuals during a deal to purchase P300,000 worth of cellphones, the Southern Police District (SPD) said on Friday.
In a statement, the SPD said the suspects were arrested along Amorsolo Street in Barangay Pio del Pilar on Thursday night following a request for police assistance from one of the victims.
Police identified the suspects only by their aliases: “Lulu,” a 27-year-old Chinese man; and “Leif” and “James,” both residents of Barangay New Lower Bicutan in Taguig City.
The victims had supposedly met with the suspects along Amorsolo Street for the transaction to purchase the cellphones.

“During the transaction, the suspects allegedly forcibly took one of the victims aboard their vehicle. The other victim pursued the vehicle and shouted for help, alerting police personnel manning a nearby post,” the SPD said.

“The police officers immediately responded, proceeded to the area, intercepted a black Ford Territory and a silver Toyota Fortuner, and arrested the three suspects before they could leave the vicinity,” it added.

Police operatives recovered a Taurus 9mm pistol with seven live rounds of ammunition; a caliber .38 revolver with three live rounds of ammunition; an unidentified number of license plates bearing different plate numbers; several cellphones and other personal belongings.
The SPD noted that authorities also recovered 1.8 grams of suspected shabu (crystal meth) worth P12,240 as well as two glass tubes with suspected drug residue from the suspects.
The three arrested individuals were taken into the custody of the Makati City Police Station.

They await charges for attempted robbery, grave coercion and usurpation of authority as well as violations of Republic Act No. 10591 or the Firearms and Ammunition Regulation Act; RA No. 9165 or the Dangerous Drugs Act; and RA No. 4136 or the Land Transportation and Traffic Code. /jpv

articles.title: Nepal-Tibet floods: two workers pulled alive from tunnel nine days after disaster
articles.summary:
Officials say pair were rescued from Trishuli 3A hydropower tunnel in Nepal after being trapped in depth of 170 metres

Two people have been pulled out alive from a hydropower tunnel in Nepal…
articles.byline: Hannah Ellis-Petersen and Gaurav Pokharel in Kathmandu

blocks.text: Two people have been pulled out alive from a hydropower tunnel in Nepal nine days after deadly flash floods buried the projects in deep mud and left them trapped.

The workers were rescued during an ongoing operation at the Trishuli 3A tunnel, a hydropower project in one of the areas worst-affected by last week’s deadly Nepal floods, according to army spokesperson Brig Gen Raja Ram Basnet.

Sanjay Shah was the first to be rescued and was taken to the Nepal army barracks in Trishuli. Another person, identified as Kabir Maharjan, was also rescued from the tunnel. They were rescued from a depth of 170 metres inside the tunnel, confirmed Basnet.
Sanjay Shah was foreman at Upper Trishuli 3A and Kabir Maharjan was a superviser.
Nepal’s army released images of Shah being pulled from the small dark entrance of a tunnel. He emerged covered in mud but conscious and was carried from the site on a rescuer’s shoulder.
Speaking to army officials after he was rescued, Shah’s first question was: “What day is it?”
Describing his ordeal, Shah said he had been in the tunnel’s control room at the time of the flood.

“Usually there would be only five or six people there but at this time there must have been around 40 to 45 people inside,” he said. “Since I was in the control room, my responsibility was to save everyone’s lives. After such an accident, I couldn’t just run away by myself. I had to save everyone.
“While trying to get everyone out, I told them that there had been a major accident at the dam and urged everyone to run. In doing so, I lost time. In the end, I couldn’t get out myself.”
To keep himself calm in the darkness of the tunnel, Shah said he spent his time chanting mantras. He said that while trapped, he had been communicating with only three or four others.
“They were communicating by shouting to each other from nearby. There could also be people inside the powerhouse. Some of them may not have been able to escape,” he said.
Officials said the two men were in stable condition and flown to a hospital in Kathmandu.
Nepal’s communication minister, Bikram Timilsina, said officials remain hopeful that more workers will be rescued. “We are waiting for the rescue of more and more people,”he wrote on social media.

Most of the hydropower projects along the Bhotekoshi and Trishuli rivers were destroyed when a surge of water, debris and mud came coursing down the valley last week, triggered by ‌the collapse of a melting glacier on the border between Nepal and China-controlled Tibet.

blocks.caption: A survivor is carried out after being rescued from inside the tunnel. Photograph: Nepal Army/Reuters

blocks.text: At least 1,287 people were killed in the floods and more than 5,000 remain missing, according to the Nepal’s disaster management agency.

Rescue efforts have increasingly centred on the hydropower tunnels, where authorities believe workers may ⁠have survived for more than a week due to air pockets. So far, more than 270 people have been rescued across several projects.

Large boulders and flood waters had deluged the hydropower tunnels, blocking off the entrances, and some were buried deep in mud. At the Upper Trishuli 3A facility, it took rescue workers almost six days to find the tunnels.

Army and specialist teams have been working round the clock to try and clear debris from the tunnel entrance. It was confirmed that voices of many people had been heard inside after a breakthrough was made on early Friday morning.
After the rescue team called out, “Don’t panic, we are rescuing you,” they received a response from inside: “OK.”

At least 557 workers are missing from the hydropower project along the Trishuli River, with about 115 believed to be trapped in the main tunnel, according to the Independent Power Producers Association of Nepal.

Families of those missing in the tunnels have been gathering at hospitals in Kathmandu and at the Nepal electricity office for nine days, desperate for answers about their relatives. Posters of workers missing in Trishuli 3A and other projects line the wall of Tribhuvan University teaching hospital in Nepal’s capital.
In total, local authorities estimate about 900 workers are missing from 12 hydropower projects high up in the Himalayas, with about 500 believed to be trapped in tunnels.
Rescue efforts have also been focused on Rasuwagadhi hydropower plant where Nepal authorities said they are confident that 46 workers trapped in an underground chamber in the plant are still alive.

articles.title: ‘This could just be the beginning’: minorities fear first far-right win in German state election
articles.summary:
As polls point to victory in Saxony-Anhalt for AfD party promising deportations, people face agonising choice: stay or go

As the Bible study session wrapped up, leaving worshippers to mingle…

blocks.text: As the Bible study session wrapped up, leaving worshippers to mingle over cake and coffee, Fatemeh, 44, fought back tears as the conversation turned to Sunday’s state election in Saxony-Anhalt.
“I worry about it every day,” she said. “I can’t stop thinking about my son and what might happen to us.”

Three years ago she fled Iran with her son after he was stopped by police during a protest over the death in police custody of Mahsa Amini. They ended up in Saxony-Anhalt, where, as they await a final decision on their asylum claim, she has watched him blossom into a gifted athlete and develop a knack for repairing vehicles.

blocks.caption: Fatemeh worries about what might happen after the elections. Photograph: Christian Jungeblodt/The Guardian

items: Fatemeh worries about what might happen after the elections. Photograph: Christian Jungeblodt/The Guardian

blocks.text: Looming over their lives, however, are the politics of Saxony-Anhalt. Polls have suggested that the election on Sunday could yield Germany’s first-ever state government led by the far-right Alternative für Deutschland (AfD), shattering a postwar taboo and leaving Fatemeh and her son’s fate in the hands of a party that has promised to launch deportations “from day one”.
That possibility has left her racked with worry. “They might send us back to Iran,” she said. “As a converted Christian, that could mean the death penalty for me.”

It was a glimpse of the stakes at play in the election. Polls suggest the state’s AfD, whose antisemitic, anti-Islam and anti-migrant discourse has contributed to authorities classifying the party as “firmly rightwing extremist”, is poised to win the most votes.

blocks.caption: The square in the centre of Magdeburg where the Christmas market attack took place on 20 December 2024. Photograph: Christian Jungeblodt/The Guardian

items: The square in the centre of Magdeburg where the Christmas market attack took place on 20 December 2024. Photograph: Christian Jungeblodt/The Guardian

blocks.text: A strong showing in the election could allow it to govern Saxony-Anhalt, turning the eastern state into Germany’s first testing ground for the AfD’s long-running hostility towards migrants, including refugees, Muslims and the LGBTQ+ community.

“We’ve never seen emotions run so high over an election,” said Undra Dreßler of Lamsa, an umbrella group for migrant organisations in the state. Calls were coming in daily, she said, as people wrestled with whether the time had come to pack up their lives and start over again somewhere else.
“People are really worried and scared,” said Dreßler. “For those with migrant backgrounds, it feels like this vote is about their right to exist and their security.”

The pages-long manifesto for the AfD in Saxony-Anhalt promises a “complete, 180-degree” overhaul of the approach to migration, from educating refugee children separately to redirecting funds earmarked for integration to a unit focused on remigration, and calling on federal officials to stop recognising Ukrainians as war refugees.

In June, Dreßler’s organisation appealed to Germany’s 15 other states, calling on them to prepare to take in refugees from Saxony-Anhalt after the election. “It’s a precautionary measure,” she said. “The social climate here is already extremely heated. We don’t know what will happen after the elections.”

blocks.caption: Left: A billboard in Magdeburg shows the AfD candidate Ulrich Siegmund and the slogan ‘everything is possible’. Photograph: Christian Jungeblodt/The Guardian. Right: Siegmund addresses delegates at the federal congress of Generation Germany, the party’s youth organisation. Photograph: Jens Schlut…

items: Left: A billboard in Magdeburg shows the AfD candidate Ulrich Siegmund and the slogan ‘everything is possible’. Photograph: Christian Jungeblodt/The Guardian. Right: Siegmund addresses delegates at the federal congress of Generation Germany, the party’s youth organisation. Photograph: Jens Schluter/AFP/Getty

blocks.text: Tensions have run high in Saxony-Anhalt since late 2024 when a Saudi man drove his car into a crowded Christmas market in Magdeburg, killing six people and injuring hundreds more.

Authorities described the attacker as an anti-Islam activist who was sympathetic to the far right. Even so, rightwing voices seized on the moment to scapegoat migrants and minorities for the ills of a state long ravaged by deindustrialisation and depopulation. In the aftermath of the attack, reports of racist attacks soared as migrants and people of colour told of being spat on, threatened and, in some cases, physically attacked.

“By mid-2025, we had received as many reports of racist insults and attacks as we did in all of 2024,” said Dreßler. “As forces on the right become stronger, everyday racism and discrimination have become part of everyday life.”

On the streets of Magdeburg, many shared their own brushes with overt racism. “When you’re on the street, some people harass you verbally,” said Kirti, 27, a student from India. “They show you the middle finger.”

blocks.caption: An AfD billboard reads ‘All for our children’. The party has promised to educate refugee children in the state separately. Photograph: Christian Jungeblodt/The Guardian

items: An AfD billboard reads ‘All for our children’. The party has promised to educate refugee children in the state separately. Photograph: Christian Jungeblodt/The Guardian

blocks.text: Kirti moved to Magdeburg just over a year ago to study for a master’s degree, becoming part of a cohort of foreign students for whom reports of racism were all too familiar. “I heard of one incident where a student was travelling on a train and people were throwing stones at the door, but the door was closed,” he said. “So people are more concerned about going out. They go out with fear, rather than feeling safe.”

A recent survey suggested that as many as 80% of people with a migration background in Saxony-Anhalt are considering leaving, said Ketevan Asatiani-Hermann, who leads the board of the Advisory Council for Integration and Migration in Magdeburg.

As questions swirl over what the AfD could realistically do if the party garners enough votes to govern alone, a chorus of voices has begun to warn of the fallout. Saxony-Anhalt is a rapidly depopulating state where the average age of 48.2 ranks as the highest in Germany. “So the fear is that we lose people because of what happens on 6 September,” said Asatiani-Hermann. “And Saxony-Anhalt is dependent on migrants, so it’s absolutely necessary that they stay here.”

blocks.caption: Ketevan Asatiani-Hermann says Saxony-Anhalt is dependent on migrants and it is ‘absolutely necessary’ they stay. Photograph: Christian Jungeblodt/The Guardian

items: Ketevan Asatiani-Hermann says Saxony-Anhalt is dependent on migrants and it is ‘absolutely necessary’ they stay. Photograph: Christian Jungeblodt/The Guardian

blocks.text: Foreign nationals account for about 9% of the state’s population – compared with approximately 15% nationwide – with many playing a critical role in sectors such as hospitality and care for elderly people.

In May, the state medical association said that more than one in four doctors working in Saxony-Anhalt’s hospitals, or 27.1%, do not hold a German passport. “In many regions of the state – especially in rural areas – comprehensive healthcare coverage would no longer be possible without foreign colleagues,” it said, citing the possibility of longer waiting times or facility closures if some of these doctors were to leave.

“Migrants make up a huge part of healthcare. If you were to take them out, the whole system would collapse,” said Hamid, 41, a paramedic originally from Iran. “So it’s like if you have a bus and you take off all the tyres. You cannot move.”

blocks.caption: Hamid, a paramedic originally from Iran, says without migrants in Magdeburg, the ‘whole system would collapse’. Photograph: Christian Jungeblodt/The Guardian

items: Hamid, a paramedic originally from Iran, says without migrants in Magdeburg, the ‘whole system would collapse’. Photograph: Christian Jungeblodt/The Guardian

blocks.text: At Magdeburg’s synagogue – whose light-filled foyer includes a mural showing one of the few remaining photographs of the original synagogue that was destroyed in a 1938 pogrom – people listed their concerns about an AfD majority, from whether it would affect the funding they receive, to what the party’s plans for a “remigration offensive” would mean for the Ukrainian refugees who had joined their congregation after Russia’s full-scale invasion.

The far-right party has also promised to make changes to the school curriculum, in what one party member described as “more Bismarck, less Hitler”. The underlying assumption was that the focus on the rise of National Socialism and the Holocaust – as opposed to the unification of Germany by Otto von Bismarck – had shifted the guilt over what had happened to the current generation, said Igor Mendel Itkin, the synagogue’s rabbi.

“They think: ‘If we get rid of this, we will feel free.’ But I think it will be the other way around,” he said. “You cannot get rid of this ghost; you can pacify it, but you cannot get rid of it. If people don’t learn about it, then something like this could happen again, maybe not with the Jewish people, but maybe with the Muslims.”

He pointed to Saxony-Anhalt’s AfD manifesto, which makes no mention of the Jewish community but includes promises to “exhaust all legal means to restrict the influence” of Islam, even as it notes that Muslims account for just 2-3% of the 2 million people in the state.

blocks.caption: Rabbi Igor Mendel Itkin with Maria Schubert at the Magdeburg synagogue say an AfD win is ‘unimaginable’. Photograph: Christian Jungeblodt/The Guardian

items: Rabbi Igor Mendel Itkin with Maria Schubert at the Magdeburg synagogue say an AfD win is ‘unimaginable’. Photograph: Christian Jungeblodt/The Guardian

blocks.text: An AfD win would put Jewish people in a complicated position, said Maria Schubert from the Synagogue Community of Magdeburg. “If they win, we don’t know how we will act with them. For me, it’s unimaginable,” she said.

She worried that it could also be a dilemma faced by others if Sunday’s election turned out to be a bellwether of shifting political forces rather than an outlier. “I see it as a threat, in that this could just be the beginning. In other German states, many are looking at Saxony-Anhalt to kick things off,” she said. “I mean, at the beginning, nobody took Hitler seriously.”
The AfD was approached for comment.
With contribution from Niclas Boenki

articles.title: Mindoro’s dramatic economic turnaround beating poverty, insurgency
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines – Improving economic conditions in the province of Occidental Mindoro has resulted in a reduction of poverty and insurgency incidents. In a statement released by the National Task…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines – Improving economic conditions in the province of Occidental Mindoro has resulted in a reduction of poverty and insurgency incidents.

In a statement released by the National Task Force to End Local Communist Armed Conflict (NTF-Elcac) on Friday, Occidental Mindoro Lone District Rep. Leody Tarriela said the province’s dramatic economic turnaround — from 2.1 percent growth to a nation-leading 11.2 percent — offers compelling evidence that bringing roads, electricity, livelihoods and basic government services to formerly conflict-affected communities can break the cycle of poverty and insurgency.

He added that the province’s transformation demonstrates in concrete terms the principle behind the government’s whole-of-nation peace and development strategy: lasting peace cannot be secured by security operations alone, but must be sustained by development that people can see, use and feel in their everyday lives.
Tarriela declared that infrastructure has opened communities once isolated by geography, poverty and decades of armed conflict.

His remarks came amid Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA) data showing Occidental Mindoro posting an extraordinary economic expansion, alongside recent statements from the National Anti-Poverty Commission and Presidential Adviser on Poverty Alleviation Secretary Larry Gadon linking poverty reduction and inclusive development with the weakening of conditions historically exploited by insurgent groups.

For decades, Occidental Mindoro was known as the country’s “brownout capital” due to chronic power interruptions lasting from 16 to 18 hours daily, while many remote communities in the province remained vulnerable to communist insurgency.
Improved power supply, expanding infrastructure and sustained peace and development interventions have helped create conditions for investment, employment and greater economic activity.
Power interruptions have been substantially reduced, while seven of the province’s 11 municipalities had attained insurgency-free status by 2024.

“The 11.2 percent growth is not just a number—it is a symbol of real change,” Tarriela said. And with improved power supply, the lawmaker said investors came to Occidental Mindoro, bringing in more jobs and opportunities.
With this development, Tarriela said poverty and hunger fell, with government services now truly felt. And this is why, Tarriela said, why people no longer join or support armed groups.
He cited the municipality of Magsaysay as a concrete example of development reaching communities on the ground.

Magsaysay became the first municipality in the country to complete an infrastructure project under the FY 2026 Local Government Support Fund–Support to the Barangay Development Program (LGSF-SBDP), making Mimaropa the first region nationwide to report completed projects under the FY 2026 program.

Under the FY 2026 SBDP, eligible cleared barangays receive funding for high-impact community projects such as farm-to-market roads, water systems, school buildings, health stations and rural electrification—investments designed to address the very conditions of isolation and underdevelopment that allowed insurgency to persist for decades.

Tarriela likewise cited Sablayan, where farm-to-market roads and other development initiatives have begun connecting previously isolated communities to markets, schools, health facilities and government services. He also explained that isolation imposes a heavy economic burden on poor communities.

“Kung maganda ang buhay ng tao at kumakain ng tatlong beses sa isang araw, nakapag-aral ang mga anak nila—doon nababawasan ang insurhensya (if the people are having a good life and eating three times a day and able to send their children to school—insurgency will be greatly reduced),” Tarriela said.

He thanked President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. and the NTF-Elcac for sustaining development interventions in communities emerging from decades of insurgency, stressing that programs such as the BDP help convert security gains into lasting economic and social progress.

Tarriela acknowledged that Occidental Mindoro still faces challenges, particularly in achieving fully reliable electricity and consolidating lasting peace across the province. But its experience, he said, demonstrates what can happen when the government addresses conflict not only through security measures, but by confronting the poverty, isolation and lack of opportunity on which insurgency has historically thrived.

He called for the expansion and sustained funding of the Barangay Development Program, saying many communities across the country are still waiting for the roads, water systems, schools, health facilities, electricity and livelihood opportunities now transforming parts of Occidental Mindoro. /jpv

articles.title: 6 arrested, 64 fake plates seized in Davao City raids
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines – Five establishments in Davao City were raided by authorities for allegedly manufacturing fake vehicle license plates on Thursday, according to the Land Transportation Office…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines – Five establishments in Davao City were raided by authorities for allegedly manufacturing fake vehicle license plates on Thursday, according to the Land Transportation Office (LTO).

In a statement on Friday, the LTO noted that six individuals allegedly involved in the scheme were arrested, while 64 fake plates were confiscated during the operation along Quezon Boulevard in Davao City.
The five establishments were identified as Pogz Art and Sign, Eschat Art and Sign Tailoring, Sticker Art and Sign, WMT Printing Services, and Magnorms Advertising Services.

The LTO implemented the raid alongside personnel from the Philippine National Police-Criminal Investigation and Detection Group, the PNP-Regional Intelligence Division 11, and the PNP-Davao City Police Office.

Authorities also seized computers, machine tools and other equipment allegedly used to manufacture the counterfeit plates, including hammers, cutters, steel plates, sticker cutters, plain sheets and an improvised flat screw used for molding.
The six arrested individuals were brought to the Davao City Police Station for documentation and proper disposition.

They will face charges for alleged violation of falsification by private individuals and use of falsified documents, manufacturing and possession of instruments or implants for falsification, and the Motorcycle Crime Prevention Act, the LTO said.
Meanwhile, the confiscated equipment and other evidence were inventoried and secured for further proceedings.
LTO chief Assistant Secretary Markus Lacanilao said the agency would go after not only motorists who use fake plates but also those who manufacture and sell them.
“Hinahanap namin kung saan ito ginagawa at kung sino ang kumikita sa ilegal na negosyong ito. Hangga’t may gumagawa at nagbebenta ng pekeng plaka, tuloy ang operasyon ng LTO,” Lacanilao said.

(We are looking for where these [fake plates] are being made and who is profiting from this illegal business. As long as someone is making and selling fake license plates, the LTO’s operations will continue.)
He urged motorists not to buy or use counterfeit license plates, including those made to resemble official LTO plates.

The LTO also advised the public to report suspected illegal manufacturing or selling of fake plates through the agency’s “I-Report Mo Kay LTO Chief” Facebook page or its website. — Rendell Ivan Manuel, INQUIRER.net trainee/ dp

articles.title: Nothing left: Nepal flood survivors face loss and uncertainty
articles.summary: Rasuwa, Nepal – In Nepal’s flood-ravaged Rasuwa district, Yangee Tamang grapples with grief and uncertainty, days after deadly torrents swept away entire villages, leaving a landscape of mud,…

blocks.text: Rasuwa, Nepal – In Nepal’s flood-ravaged Rasuwa district, Yangee Tamang grapples with grief and uncertainty, days after deadly torrents swept away entire villages, leaving a landscape of mud, rock and debris.
From a helicopter flying up the valley of destruction, the ground below resembles a puzzle with missing pieces. Entire sections of settlements have vanished.
Picturesque villages of green paddy fields and houses sit beside vast chunks of land washed away.
Tamang’s house sits on a hillside in Syabrubesi in Rasuwa district, but the flood swept away the settlement below, where her relatives lived and markets were.
“It is all gone, nothing is left. No one is left,” Tamang told AFP, after tracing the route of the August 26 destruction by air on Thursday, with roads below washed out.
Rescue teams in Nepal have recovered more than 1,250 bodies, and more than 5,000 are missing, after the gigantic wave triggered by a rock and ice avalanche roared down the China-Nepal border.
What were once busy villages, markets, green hillsides and winding roads in Rasuwa have been transformed into vast stretches of mud, broken rock and debris.
“It wasn’t really water, it was gas-like, all black and it moved like boiling water,” she said.
“It was all so sudden, it was not possible for anyone to run away.”
About 100 people are feared trapped in hydropower tunnels.
Tamang’s husband is safe, but his workplace, the nearby Chilime Hydropower Project, which was smashed by the flood.
“I don’t know what we will do. Nothing is left here for us to live,” she said.
The river, still flowing brown, traces a path of destruction, and the enormous amount of debris has changed the shape and course of the waterways.
The floodwaters, carrying huge quantities of mud and rocks, rushed through river valleys with tremendous force.
In narrow gorges between the lush green hills, soil lies exposed where the flood stripped away trees and grass.
Roads that once connected remote communities have been washed away, while bridges lie destroyed or have completely disappeared.
Vehicles remain stranded on washed-out roads along hillsides.
Along the route, many surviving buildings are buried beneath thick layers of mud.
Some remain standing but are left empty, the people gone.
Risang Tamang, another resident, said for those left, the future is bleak.
“It is difficult — roads are is such a state, so many bridges have been swept away. Now, even if you have money, there is nowhere to buy anything,” he told AFP.
“Any hope that we can live here has died.” /dp

articles.title: Argentina: Milei reignites dispute over Falkland Islands
articles.summary: The Argentine leader said that a change in the US's position on the Falkland Islands could be coming, which would alter the US's years-long neutrality on the issue.

image.caption: The Falkland Islands have been the subject of a dispute between Britain and Argentina [FILE: January 2009]Image: Dreamstime/IMAGO

blocks.text: Argentine President Javier Milei said the US' position on the Falkland Islands could be changing.
He added that his country would impose sanctions on any oil companies operating in the British overseas territory.

In a nationally televised speech on Thursday, Milei reiterated Argentina's stance that the Falkland Islands are part of its territory. This move could further escalate the long-standing dispute with Britain over the islands.

The Argentine leader also praised President Donald Trump's comments regarding the US potentially revisiting its largely neutral position on the Falklands, saying this is a result of his close relationship with Trump.
According to Milei, the US is considering this change in position due to Argentina being a "reliable partner, aligned with Western values" that can be "a valuable ally in the decades to come."

blocks.caption: Argentine President Javier Milei (right) praised his relationship with US President Donald Trump [FILE: October 2025]Image: Jonathan Ernst/REUTERS

blocks.text: Milei announced several moves aimed at stopping the Sea Lion oil project, which is located about 140 miles from the islands — an area that Argentina considers its own. Two companies, one from the UK and one from Israel, plan to begin drilling in the area in the coming months with the goal of producing oil by 2028.
"Argentina will not stand idly by," Milei said, adding that any further advance on the Islands will be viewed as a "violation of our national security."
The Falklands issue is a point of consensus in an Argentine society divided by political differences in other areas.
Britain 'unwavering' position unchanged
Meanwhile, British Prime Minister Andy Burnham's spokesperson said the British government's position was "long-standing and unwavering."
"Sovereignty rests with the UK, and the islanders' right to self-determination is paramount,” he said.

Any change in the US' neutral approach towards the dispute between Britain and Argentina would be a major shift and could contribute to further deterioration in already strained transatlantic relations.
Asked about whether his administration could change its position on the Falkland Islands, Trump said he "always" reviews positions.
"That's just one of many," he added.
In another interview, Trump was asked whether the US would come to help Britain should it be involved in an armed conflict over the islands.
"Your country was not there to help me," he answered, referring to Britain's refusal to take an active part in the joint US-Israeli campaign against Iran.
Trump's bailout push for Milei sways Argentina's politics

articles.title: EV sales outpace petrol cars for first time as Australians dodge soaring fuel costs
articles.summary: New record for Australia as more than 27,000 EVs sold in August, driven by the rising cost of fuel and new government policy

blocks.text: Electric vehicle sales in Australia exceeded petrol cars for the first time last month as a transformation driven by high fuel prices and government policy encouraging clean car uptake accelerated.

More than 27,000 EVs were sold in August, a new record for a single month and representing 24.9% of new cars sold. The climate-friendly technology surpassed both petrol vehicles (nearly 26,000 sold) and diesel cars (23,600).
If plug-in hybrids were added, the proportion of new cars with a plug jumped to 36% of sales.

The rise in EVs has been helped by two factors – the war in Iran pushing up oil prices and making running a petrol car significantly more expensive, and the introduction last year of a federal vehicle emissions standard that required auto companies to cut average tailpipe emissions year-on-year. The latter has triggered a big increase in the number of models of low and zero-emission cars available at a range of prices.

Australia had previously trailed most OECD countries in EV take-up, and the technology has been the focus of political scare campaigns, including former prime minister Scott Morrison claiming in 2019 that introducing a vehicle emissions standard would “end the weekend”. They made up less than 2% of sales just four years ago and about 8% last year.
The climate change and energy minister, Chris Bowen, said EV sales surpassing petrol cars was a “landmark moment”.

“Australians have seen through the scare campaigns and are voting with their wallets for cars that are cheaper to run, cleaner and reduce their exposure to international petrol price shocks,” he said.

Toyota was Australians’ most popular car brand in August, followed by Chinese EV manufacturer BYD and trillionaire Elon Musk’s Tesla. Five of the top 10 brands were Chinese: BYD, GWM, MG, Geely and Cheery. The Tesla Model Y was the most popular new model, with more than 6,400 sold.
The Electric Vehicle Council said there had been a “structural shift in the way Australians choose their cars”, with both economic and environmental benefits driving the change.
after newsletter promotion

The council’s chief executive, Julie Delvecchio, said there were now nearly 200 EV models on offer. “The priority now is to make the benefits of going electric accessible to more Australians, including people in regional communities, apartment residents and the 30% of Australians who rent their home,” she said.
The Federal Chamber of Automotive Industries CEO, Tony Weber, said consumer choice and competition were rapidly reshaping the new-vehicle market and infrastructure settings needed to keep pace.
“Accessible and dependable charging will remain critical to consumer confidence, particularly on highways, in rural and regional areas and for motorists without access to charging at home,” he said.

blocks.text: The impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte — the first Philippine public official to be impeached twice by the House of Representatives — began at 2 pm on Monday, July 6.

There are four articles of impeachment against Duterte involving alleged misuse of confidential funds, unexplained wealth, bribery of Department of Education officials, and grave threats against President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. and his family.

Only 21 out of 24 senator-judges are physically present. Senator Bato dela Rosa remains in hiding as he faces an International Criminal Court arrest warrant over Rodrigo Duterte’s drug war, Senator Jinggoy Estrada has been detained and suspended in connection with a plunder case, and Senator Rodante Marcoleta surrendered to authorities as he also faces a plunder case.

articles.title: FIFA accuses UEFA of 'smear campaign' against Infantino
articles.summary: The dispute between the two football associations reached a US court, in which UEFA is looking for permission to collect evidence for criminal proceedings in Switzerland.

image.caption: UEFA President Aleksander Ceferin (left) and FIFA President Gianni Infantino have been at odds [FILE: June 2024]Image: Nick Potts/PA Images/IMAGO

blocks.text: World football governing body FIFA took a lash at Europe's UEFA for starting a "smear campaign" and "fishing expedition" against FIFA and its President Gianni Infantino.

This comes after a dispute between the two organizations due to FIFA's plan to sell a stake in its commercial rights, with UEFA submitting an ex parte application to the US District Court in New York to obtain testimony and documents from US-based entities. These documents will be used in potential criminal proceedings in Switzerland, where both FIFA and UEFA are based.

"While these applications are styled as legal pleadings with captions and docket numbers, they are little more than press releases in further support of UEFA’s smear campaign against FIFA and its leadership,” FIFA said in a filing in US District Court in Colorado on Thursday.
FIFA's filing in Colorado was a motion to intervene, requesting that the discovery process be postponed or dismissed.

blocks.caption: Spain won the 2026 FIFA World Cup [FILE: July 2026]Image: Evrim Aydin/Anadolu/picture alliance

blocks.text: According to UEFA, the FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE), an entity which would have had the commercial rights linked over the FIFA World Cup to investors was developed without adequate consulting FIFA's 211 member associations, as well as FIFA's own governing bodies.
UEFA threatened to boycott the FIFA World Cup should the move go ahead.
The move would have affected both the men's and the women's tournaments.
FIFA argued that the association representing European football had tried to scupper the proposal with a bid to keep European football's dominance as is.
Demands for Infatino's resignation
Pressure has been mounting on both FIFA and its President Gianni Infantino since the FFE plans were made public.

blocks.caption: Criticism is mounting over FIFA's now-scrapped plans to sell a stake in the World Cup's commercial rights  [FILE: May 2026]Image: Ethan Cairns/ZUMA/IMAGO

blocks.text: This resulted in several countries saying they will not support Infantino's reelection for a fourth term as president in March 2027, when the Swiss-born FIFA boss looks for a fourth term in office.
Aside from UEFA, two other continental confederations demand Infantino's resignation.

Both CONCACAF, representing North and Central America and the Caribbean, and the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) voiced their objections to Infantino. Only the South American and African confederations still support him.
UEFA also demanded a "genuinely independent external review" of how the proposal came about.
"FIFA cannot investigate itself and expect the football community to simply accept its conclusions," UEFA said.

articles.title: Molly Ticehurst’s killer called woman he’d met on Tinder after stabbing and said ‘I’m sorry I murdered her’, court hears
articles.summary: Daniel Billings said ‘I did what I did’ in call from friend’s house after 2024 domestic violence murder

blocks.text: Two hours after Daniel Billings murdered his ex-girlfriend Molly Ticehurst in a frenzied stabbing he spoke to a woman he had met on Tinder.
“I’m sorry I murdered her,” Billings told the woman during a phone call at 2.02am on 22 April 2024.
The woman, who Billings met on the dating app in early 2022, told police she was shocked as he described the murder during their brief conversation.

“In an ideal world, what I wanted to do was go over there and talk to her, but she started screaming and I did what I did,” Billings said, according to her statement tendered to his New South Wales supreme court sentencing hearing.
He made the phone call from a mutual friend’s property, where Billings had fled in his bloodied clothes, according to a statement of facts.
The friend soon alerted police, the court heard.
Billings, a former mine worker, has pleaded guilty to stabbing Molly Ticehurst 15 times after breaking into her bedroom at her Forbes home just before midnight on 21 April.
The 31-year-old is facing a two-day sentencing hearing in Orange that was expected to conclude on Friday.

blocks.caption: Molly Ticehurst with her mother, Kate, and father, Tony. Photograph: Supplied by the Ticehurst family

blocks.text: Billings had been released on bail by a local court registrar a fortnight before the murder. He was charged with a series of sexual assault and domestic violence offences against 28-year-old Molly.
As soon as he learned of her allegations of repeated rapes, Billings adamantly denied the crimes and developed a twisted obsession with clearing his name, the court has been told.
Thursday’s hearing heard 90 minutes of footage that Billings recorded before and after the murder, in which he repeatedly claimed to have been wrongly accused of rape.
Even as Molly Ticehurst lay dead in her pyjamas, he continued to claim he was a victim of injustice.
“I can’t believe I just did that,” he said in a video recorded immediately after the stabbing.
Billings was then seen raising a bloodied hand to his face as he drove away also appearing to retch.
“I don’t know why she accused me of rape, I don’t know what her game plan was.”
The videos appeared to allude to a plan that he would take his own life after killing Molly.

Forensic psychiatrist Olav Nielssen, engaged by the defence team, told the court many of the recordings could be interpreted as “goodbye videos” and that Billings was suffering significant depression.
But Prof David Greenberg, the crown’s expert, told the court that Billings’ threats of suicide could also be interpreted in the context of his months of domestic abuse against Molly.
“Several times he threatens the victim and her family,” Greenberg told the court on Friday. “The acts of domestic violence have the context of these suicide threats.”
The sexual assault charges were ultimately dropped when Billings pleaded guilty to murder in November 2025 after 18 months of legal negotiations
Billings listened to the proceedings on Friday in an elevated wooden dock, often leaning down to stare at the floor. He occasionally shook his head.
The court heard victim impact statements from Molly’s family on Thursday.
“When she died, part of me died with her,” her father, Tony Ticehurst, said.
Justice Natalie Adams has indicated she would sentence Billings later in September.

articles.title: Marcos signs law expanding aid for college, vocational students
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. on Friday signed into law amendments to the Universal Access to Quality Tertiary Education Act (UAQTEA), expanding government assistance for…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. on Friday signed into law amendments to the Universal Access to Quality Tertiary Education Act (UAQTEA), expanding government assistance for tertiary and vocational education students.

The new law, which will be known as Republic Act No. 12325, strengthens RA No. 10931, which provides free tuition and other school fees for students at state universities and colleges, local universities and colleges, and state-run technical-vocational institutions.

RA 12325 expands coverage under the Tertiary Education Subsidy and provides additional assistance to students from disadvantaged and underserved groups, including qualified beneficiaries of the Pantawid Pamilyang Pilipino Program.
The law will also cover more education-related expenses to help more Filipinos pursue tertiary education.

“It is a measure that builds on the government’s promise and strengthens it for the years to come—bringing us closer to a future where every Filipino family has at least one child who completes a bachelor’s degree or a technical-vocational education and training (TVET) program,” Marcos said in his speech.

“Poor and deserving students taking priority programs who are not covered by existing grants may also receive government support to pursue their studies in qualified private higher education and technical-vocational institutions,” he also said.

Marcos said education will remain at the top of his administration’s priorities, noting that every learner who completes a college degree or TVET program brings greater opportunities to their family and strengthens the country.
He also cited improvements in the country’s global standing in education.

“In 2022, only 12 of our local colleges made it to the World University Rankings for Innovation. Today, 140 of our colleges have made it into the same rankings. This is a result of deliberate choices that have been made by government,” he said.

The total proposed budget for the education sector is P1.314 trillion to P1.326 trillion under the P7.2-trillion 2027 National Expenditure Program. As mandated by the Constitution, the education sector receives the largest portion of the national budget. /jpv

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Former Public Works and Highways Secretary Manuel “Manny” Bonoan was released from the Philippine National Police’s (PNP) custody on Friday, following an order from the Sandiganbayan Fifth Division.

Bonoan was turned over by the PNP–Criminal Investigation and Detection Group National Capital Region (CIDG NCR) to his family and left the PNP General Hospital (PNPGH) in Camp Crame at around 10:35 a.m.
The court had directed the PNPGH, where Bonoan had been under hospital arrest due to several ailments since his surrender last June, to release him following the recall of his commitment order.

On Tuesday, the Fifth Division had granted a motion by state prosecutors to exclude Bonoan from the graft and plunder charges against him, Sen. Jose “Jinggoy” Estrada and three former DPWH district engineers.
The move was part of a bid to turn Bonoan into a state witness for flood control scandal cases.

Estrada, then-South Manila District Engineering Office (DEO) chief Manny Bulusan, then-Quezon City 1st DEO chief Arturo Gonzales Jr. and then-North Manila DEO assistant chief Denryl Caesar Cortuna are accused of amassing a total of P573.75 million in kickbacks through projects included in the 2025 national budget. /jpv

articles.title: Argentine leader says oil firms working off Falklands face sanctions
articles.summary: Javier Milei reiterates his country's claim on the British overseas territory, saying the "winds of change" favour it.

blocks.text: Argentina's President, Javier Milei, has heightened tensions with the UK over the Falklands, warning he will impose economic sanctions on firms which exploit oil close to the British overseas territory.
In a national address, Milei said the "winds of change" favoured Argentina's claim to the islands, emboldened by signs the US might reconsider its stance of neutrality on the issue.
Milei said the Sea Lion oilfield, where a British and an Israeli firm are due to begin exploration work, was a "clear and present danger".
More than 40 years after the war over the territory, sovereignty of the archipelago in the south-west Atlantic Ocean remains hotly disputed between Britain and Argentina.
BBC News is seeking comment from the UK government on Milei's statement. It reiterated this week that Falkland islanders "are British with a right to determine their own future".
Milei announced his sanctions plan surrounded by his cabinet at the presidential palace, reiterating that the Falklands were "historically and legally" Argentinean.
The crux was a proposal to introduce a bill to parliament to impose sanctions on energy firms planning to begin oil exploration off the Falklands.
The Sea Lion oilfield, around 130 miles from the islands, contains an estimated 1.7 billion barrels of oil.

Two oil companies – Britain's Rockhopper Exploration and Israel's Navitas Petroleum – are due to begin exploration work in the Sea Lion oilfield off the Falklands coast within two years, something Milei said Argentina could not allow.
"If we do not act swiftly in a few months, they will have the material capacity to access the oil that lies underneath our sea – something that has never happened before," Milei said.

It is not yet clear how or to what extent the sanctions will be imposed or tightened. In Argentina, a current law already allows for restrictions of activities of oil companies participating in projects considered unauthorised on the islands.
In a 2013 referendum, residents of the islands voted overwhelmingly to remain a British overseas territory - with 99.8% voting in favour and just three voting against.

When asked in an interview with GB News earlier on Thursday if the US would "come to the UK's aid" during a potential territorial dispute, Trump replied that Britain had "not been there to help me" with his country's war with Iran.
Trump's latest remarks come after he previously said the US could revise its neutral position on the islands' sovereignty if the UK failed to increase defence spending.

Milei also announced plans for a naval base in Tierra del Fuego in the south of Argentina, saying Trump and the US were "assessing their historical position in regard to the Falklands", which Argentina refers to as Las Malvinas.
"That is not empty words as they understand that Argentina is a reliable partner and a valuable ally for decades to come," he said, describing the UK as a nation "in decline".
"There are winds of change in the world that are favourable to our claim," Milei added.

Hours before Milei's speech, Sarah Rogers, a senior official in the US state department, posted a photo of herself with Milei alongside the caption: "Exciting things are happening in the Western Hemisphere."
Argentine forces landed on the Falklands to stake a territorial claim in 1982, sparking a 74-day war over the territory as a British military task force ejected them.
The conflict led to the deaths of 255 British military personnel, three islanders and 649 Argentine military personnel.

In a sign of the ongoing tensions between the two countries over the issue, Argentina players celebrated their victory over England in the World Cup by waving a banner in support of their country's territorial claim.

articles.title: Blue Jays close in on Guardians in wild-card chase, but Cleveland has an extra game to play
articles.summary: The Toronto Blue Jays have nearly closed the gap with the Cleveland Guardians in the battle for the American League's remaining wild-card spot, but they'll have to work to keep it that way — and hope…

image.caption: Catcher Brandon Valenzuela, left, and Vladimir Guerrero Jr. celebrate the Jays' 6-3 win over the Cleveland Guardians at Progressive Field on Thursday afternoon. (Nick Cammett/Getty Images)

blocks.text: MLB·New

The Toronto Blue Jays have nearly closed the gap with the Cleveland Guardians in the battle for the American League's remaining wild-card spot, but they'll have to work to keep it that way — and hope the Guardians lose at least once in their Friday double-header.
Guardians will play a double-header against the Detroit Tigers on Friday
Toronto (70-71) and Cleveland (70-70) have the same number of wins heading into Friday's games, but the Guardians will get a couple chances to add to that as they play two against the Detroit Tigers.

If the Guardians win both games against the Tigers, they'd finish the day at 72-70. The best Toronto can do is to bank a win against the Kansas City Royals on Friday and improve to 71-71 — putting them back at the .500 mark for the first time since June.
The Blue Jays, Guardians and a handful of other teams are all fighting for the third AL wild-card.
Jays win series with Guardians
Cleveland and Toronto battled it out in a three-game series this week, with the Jays winning two of three — including their 6-3 victory Thursday afternoon.

The Blue Jays start a three-game series with the Kansas City on Friday. Toronto has 21 games left to play in the regular season and needs to keep stacking up victories for their playoff hopes to stay alive.
Six American League teams will advance to the post-season — three division winners, and the three teams with the next-best records that are awarded wild-card spots.
The New York Yankees and Boston Red Sox have the best records outside of the division leading Tampa Bay Rays, and currently occupy two of those spots.
The Texas Rangers won on Thursday, improving to 70-71 and keeping pace with the Blue Jays.
The Baltimore Orioles, meanwhile, lost to Boston on Thursday, putting the team at 69-72 on the season.

Geoff Nixon is a writer on CBC's national digital desk in Toronto. He has covered a wealth of topics, from real estate to technology to world events.

articles.title: Northern Samar Prov’l Hospital limits referrals amid bed shortage
articles.summary: TACLOBAN CITY—The Northern Samar Provincial Hospital (NSPH) has exceeded its maximum bed capacity, prompting the provincial government-run facility to ask partner health facilities and the public to…

blocks.text: TACLOBAN CITY—The Northern Samar Provincial Hospital (NSPH) has exceeded its maximum bed capacity, prompting the provincial government-run facility to ask partner health facilities and the public to limit referrals to patients needing specialized or higher-level medical care.
In a public advisory on Thursday, NSPH reported 372 total bed admissions, compared with its 302 implementing beds and the 150-bed capacity authorized by the Department of Health (DOH).
The hospital, which is based in Catarman, said it currently has no available beds for additional admissions as it continues to operate beyond its maximum capacity.
NSPH appealed to partner hospitals, health facilities, and the public to refer or bring to the provincial hospital only patients who need specialized or higher-level care services.

It also asked referring facilities to stabilize patients before dispatch to NSPH to help ensure patients arrive in a condition suitable for transport and that available resources can be prioritized for critical and emergency cases.
The hospital said the cooperation of referring facilities and the public is needed to ensure that patients with critical and emergency conditions receive immediate and appropriate medical attention.
The NSPH is Northern Samar’s main referral hospital, serving patients from various municipalities across the province.
The provincial government also operates eight district hospitals across Northern Samar, each with a capacity ranging from 50 to 100 beds.

Hospital bed capacity refers to the number of beds available for patient care. When admissions exceed a facility’s capacity, hospitals may not be able to take in new patients, particularly those requiring emergency or specialized services.

In such situations, referring hospitals are generally expected to provide initial assessment and stabilization, when medically appropriate, before transferring patients to a higher-level facility. This reduces risks during patients’ transport and allows the receiving hospital to prepare for those who require specialized care./coa

articles.title: Rainfall helps reduce air pollution from Indonesia wildfire – Pagasa
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Rainfall is a factor in lowering air pollution levels linked to the wildfire in Indonesia, according to a Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Rainfall is a factor in lowering air pollution levels linked to the wildfire in Indonesia, according to a Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration (Pagasa) specialist.

In a phone interview with the Inquirer on Friday, Pagasa specialist John Manalo noted that the direction of the winds carrying the air pollutants was more leaning toward the Visayas and Mindanao as the southwest monsoon (habagat) continued to prevail over parts of Luzon.
“Yung mga pag-ulan na associated sa habagat ay nakakatulong para mas mabawasan yung concentration ng mga air pollutants. Mayroong pollutant deposition na nangyayari,” Manalo explained.
(Rains associated with the southwest monsoon will help in reducing the concentration of air pollutants. Pollutant deposition occurs.)
“Yung epekto nito sa respiratory system ng mga makakalangap ay bahagyang mababawasan yung air pollution na malalanghap nila dahil din sa mga pag-ulan na yun,” he added.
(The effect on the respiratory system of those who breathe in this air is slightly reduced because of those rains.)
The southwest monsoon was forecast to bring rains over the western section of Luzon on Friday, Manalo said, adding that the rains may decrease over the weekend.

Currently, air quality monitoring stations in all 16 cities and the lone municipality in the National Capital Region showed low PM2.5 air pollution levels between 20 and 41 as of 6 a.m. on Friday, according to data from the Environmental Management Bureau (EMB).
Further, air quality monitoring stations in Meycauayan, Bulacan; and Santa Cruz, Zambales showed low PM2.5 air pollution levels between 17 and 35 as of 9 a.m. on Friday.
PM2.5 refers to fine particulate matter measuring 2.5 micrometers or less in diameter.

“Mababa yung air pollutants dahil sa pag-ulan for a certain period of time. Kapag kasi naging dry ulit, magkakaroon ulit ng dispersion and then possibly na naman umabot ng Luzon [yung pollutants],” Manalo explained.
(Air pollutants are lowered due to the rains for a certain period of time. Once it’s dry again, there will be dispersion and the pollutants may possibly reach Luzon.)
Meanwhile, according to Manalo, only isolated or scattered rain showers were forecast for most of the Visayas and Mindanao on Friday.
“Pero, dahil localized lang, yung magiging epekto nung pagkababa ng air pollutants dahil sa pag-ulan ay limited lang din dun sa area mismo kung saan umulan,” he added.
(But, because it’s localized, the effect on the lowering of air pollutants due to the rain may also be limited in the area where the rain occurs.)
International media have reported that the fire in Indonesia has burned in recent weeks and may be exacerbated by a looming stronger El Niño. /jpv

articles.title: Heated Rivalry casts Resident Evil's Milla Jovovich, Gossip Girl's Kevin Zegers in Season 2
articles.summary: The cast of Heated Rivalry is getting hotter by the week, with the Canadian-made hockey drama recruiting three more stars for its second season roster.

image.caption: Actors Kevin Zegers, Paul Gross and Milla Jovovich are the newest cast members of Heated Rivalry's hotly anticipated second season. (Bell Media)

blocks.text: Entertainment·New
The cast of Heated Rivalry is getting hotter by the week, with the Canadian-made hockey drama recruiting three more stars for its second season roster.
Due South star Paul Gross also joins smash hit hockey drama shooting in Greater Toronto, other areas

Heated Rivalry, a production of Bell Media's Crave streaming service, became a global phenomenon in its inaugural six-episode season, after being picked up by HBO in the U.S. and internationally, and catapulted the careers of its lead stars — B.C.-born Hudson Williams, U.S. actor Connor Storrie and Quebec's François Arnaud.
Rookie cast members announced Thursday include:

items: Ukrainian-American actress Milla Jovovich, star of the Resident Evil franchise and Luc Besson's sci-fi classic The Fifth Element.
Kevin Zegers, originally from Woodstock, Ont., who had a recurring role in the CW series Gossip Girl, Paramount+'s The Madison and films such as Transamerica.
And, Canadian film, television and theatre stalwart Paul Gross, known for the CTV-CBS series Due South and the films Men With Brooms and Passchendaele, both of which he also wrote and directed.

blocks.text: "I'm so glad I don't have to keep these three a secret any more," Nova Scotia author Rachel Reid, whose Game Changers books inspired the streaming series, commented on an Instagram post about the casting announcement.
Heated Rivalry author Rachel Reid just made a big donation to rural libraries. Here's why
The series follows the secret romance between two young rivals on the rink — Shane Hollander (Williams) and Ilya Rozanov (Storrie) — as their careers are taking off.
Gross, who recently starred in the Stratford Festival production of Samuel Beckett's Waiting for Godot, is set to play hockey league commissioner Roger Crowell.
Zegers will play Coach Wiebe, head of the Ottawa Centaurs — the fictitious team Hollander plays for.
Jovovich will take on the role of Dr. Galina Molchalina, a Russian-speaking therapist who supports Rozanov.
"Let's bring up the heat baby," Jovovich said on her Instagram account.
New cast includes Schitt's Creek star
Bell Media previously announced that Season 1 actors Robbie G.K., Sophie Nélisse, Christina Chang and Dylan Walsh, among others, would return to their roles.
The production has also drafted an array of Canadian talent for the new season, including:

items: New Brunswick-born Charlie Gillespie will star as Ottawa Centaurs forward Troy Barrett, who falls for team social media manager Harris Drover, played by American actor Justice Smith.
Daniel Diemer, known for Percy Jackson and the Olympians, is cast as hockey player Ryan Price who falls for aspiring musician Fabian Salah, played by Welsh actor Shaheen Jafargholi.
Schitt's Creek star Emily Hampshire, who grew up in the Montreal area, joins as sex shop worker Vanessa, a confidante to Fabian.
Canada's Drag Race Season 1 winner Priyanka is in the role of Tarek, a friend of Vanessa and Fabian.
Heated Rivalry Season 2 cast announcement sparks criticism from some fans over body diversity

blocks.text: Hampshire, in an interview with CBC Montreal's Let's Go last week, said that series creator and director Jacob Tierney is one of her "oldest and bestest friends."

"I've been in every single one of his things, so it would be sad if I wasn't in this one," she told host Sabrina Marandola, noting that she actually made an uncredited voiceover appearance in the show's first season.

Hampshire said the phenomenon of Heated Rivalry is beyond anything she saw with Schitt's Creek, the CBC show that also garnered a huge international audience and went on to sweep every major comedy category at the 2020 Primetime Emmy awards in its final season.
LISTEN | Heated Rivalry's Emily Hampshire on going from one Canadian hit series to another:
Let's Go10:32In conversation with Schitt's Creek and Heated Rivalry star Emily Hampshire
Despite its popularity, Heated Rivalry is not eligible for this year's Primetime Emmys, but Storrie is up for his first-ever award for his hosting gig on Saturday Night Live in February.
Heated Rivalry did, however, dominate this year's Canadian Screen Awards, collecting 13 statuettes, including the prize for best drama and Williams's win for best lead performer.
Tierney confirmed on Aug. 17 that shooting of the second season had begun. It's set to premiere on Crave in Spring 2027.

articles.title: Pacific leaders issue joint rebuke over China missile test
articles.summary: KOROR, Palau – Pacific Island nations condemned a Chinese missile test into their midst in a joint statement agreed Thursday, despite pressure from Beijing on Palau, the host of a regional…

blocks.text: KOROR, Palau – Pacific Island nations condemned a Chinese missile test into their midst in a joint statement agreed Thursday, despite pressure from Beijing on Palau, the host of a regional leaders’ meeting.

The Pacific Islands Forum summit communique, read by Palau’s President Surangel Whipps to a late-night news conference, calls for at least 24 hours’ notice of any intercontinental ballistic missile testing.
The statement was agreed by 17 of 18 forum members, with Naoero, formerly known as Nauru, dissenting.

China gave only a handful of nations short notice before test-firing the intercontinental ballistic missile in July, flexing its military might in a region where it has long sought to expand its influence.

The missile landed in international waters near Taiwan ally Tuvalu and Naoero, sparking immediate outrage from Pacific countries who hold bitter memories of nuclear testing by the US, Britain and France decades earlier, and have declared their waters a nuclear free zone.
The summit’s communique says leaders “register concern on the recent intercontinental ballistic missile (ICBM) test which overflew a number of members without adequate notice”.

It called on “all states undertaking ICBM testing to ensure transparency and reassurance including through the provision of advanced notification of a test, at least 24 hours, in accordance with international practice”.
Beijing said the test launch was “a routine arrangement of China’s annual military training”, and that “relevant countries were informed in advance”.
Naoero switched diplomatic ties from Taiwan to Beijing two years ago, and has been reluctant to criticise China, a significant infrastructure lender to the region.
On Thursday, the Chinese foreign ministry accused Palau of “hijacking” responses from other Pacific nations.

“Palau has repeatedly hyped the issue, maliciously hijacking the positions of other Pacific Islands Forum member countries. This scheme will not succeed,” ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun told a news conference in Beijing, before the Pacific statement.
“I think the message from the forum is clear, transparency needs to happen,” Whipps responded.

The United States conducts ballistic missile tests in the Pacific under a defence agreement with the Marshall Islands, which Palau and Australia’s leaders said Thursday was “very different” to China’s test because adequate notice is given.

Palau invited its diplomatic ally Taiwan to the forum as an aid partner, among a dozen non-Pacific countries including China and the United States that participate in sideline events in different capacities.
Beijing bristled at the presence of Taiwan Foreign Minister Lin Chia-lung at the opening ceremony.
Beijing claims self-ruled Taiwan as part of its territory, and China’s Pacific envoy Qian Bo told reporters on Monday there would be “consequences”.
Taiwan hit back saying its role in the Pacific, where it has three diplomatic allies, stops China from “having full control”.
The friction at times overshadowed Pacific nations’ focus on the region’s most pressing issues, tackling climate change and transnational crime.

Australia, the largest forum member and the Pacific’s biggest aid donor, pledged AU$600 million ($432 million) to boost satellite and drone aerial surveillance to help track and intercept “narco subs” bringing increasing volumes of methamphetamine and cocaine through island waters.

Papua New Guinea Prime Minister James Marape said he had raised concerns about new US visa bond charges for Pacific citizens travelling to the United States in a sideline meeting with US Deputy Secretary of State Christopher Landau.
Landau pledged $60 million to improve fuel security in the Pacific, to alleviate soaring prices caused by the Middle East crisis.
At the forum’s closing ceremony, secretary-general Baron Waqa said the Pacific faced significant challenges and had shown it would act together.
“The bonds between us must remain stronger than the forces that seek to divide us,” he said./dp

articles.title: UN to vote on adopting new world map that shows Africa’s true scale
articles.summary:
Togo-sponsored resolution calls to phase out traditional map that depicts continent as similar size to Greenland

The UN general assembly will vote on Friday on a resolution for the world to…

blocks.text: The UN general assembly will vote on Friday on a resolution for the world to formally phase out the traditional Mercator map of the globe in favour of one that more accurately displays Africa’s size.

Robert Dussey, Togo’s foreign affairs minister, said the resolution was sponsored by Togo and backed by countries including the African Union’s 54 other member states. He did not specify the total number.

blocks.caption: The 1569 map by Gerardus Mercator (1512-1594) has remained the global standard. Photograph: Stock Montage/Getty Images

blocks.text: “This discussion is not a political discussion [but] a scientific discussion, because there is scientific proof so we all have to accept the reality,” he said.

UN resolutions are non-enforceable but if the vote passes, it could lead to an update of classroom curriculums and everyday technology, given the wide usage of the Mercator projection in education, technology and governance.
The layout was introduced by the Flemish cartographer Gerardus Mercator in 1569 to help sailors navigate the seas. Almost five centuries later it remains the global standard.

Because of its projection style, however, regions near the equator appear significantly smaller than they are, whereas high-latitude areas look much larger. For example, the map shows Africa as being similar in size to Greenland, but the continent is 14 times larger than the Danish territory.

“You could fit the United States, China, India, Japan, Mexico and much of Europe into Africa and still have land to spare,” says a petition on Change.org for the #CorrectTheMap campaign, which has more than 11,000 signatures. The African Union endorsed the campaign in August 2025 and then asked Togo to spearhead its adoption.
Historians and geographers have said for years that the Mercator projection is rooted in western stereotypes. Activists have echoed this, with some coining the term “cartographic colonialism”.

Some argue that the map has subtly shaped international power dynamics by minimising the physical presence of the global south and visually inflating northern hemisphere nations while shrinking equatorial regions. This, they say, has reinforced systemic biases in international trade, development priorities and educational frameworks.

One of the Mercator projection’s most prominent critics was Arno Peters, a German historian, who launched the Peters world map based on the Gall–Peters projection in 1973. It has often been used as an alternative to the Mercator map.

blocks.caption: The 2018 Equal Earth Map. Photograph: equal-earth.com

blocks.text: Togo’s #CorrectTheMap campaign is promoting the use of the more accurate 2018 Equal Earth design, which was developed by an international team of cartographers. Supporters say it will help to reverse perceptions of Africa and decolonise global curriculums.

Some analysts agree too. JJ Enoch, a London-based senior associate at JS Held, a geopolitical risk advisory firm, said the Mercator projection visually diminished Africa’s true scale. He linked the campaign to a quest by African nations for “greater influence in global institutions and greater control over how the continent is represented”.

He added: “Adopting an equal-area map … would provide a more accurate basis for education and public understanding, while signalling that Africa’s demographic, economic and geopolitical importance should no longer be viewed through inherited and distorted conventions.”

blocks.caption: A map of Africa from Mercator's atlas dating between 1595-1602. Photograph: Royal Geographical Society/Getty Images

blocks.text: Togolese authorities hope the vote will go the same way as another African Union-backed decision at the UN this year. In March a Ghana-sponsored resolution to describe the slave trade as “gravest crime against humanity” passed, with 123 states voting in favour. Three states voted no and 52 abstained.

Ghana’s success has given supporters of the map cause to believe in a favourable outcome. Togo’s government is planning an event in Lomé, the Togolese capital, with Unesco, the African Union and tech brands such as Google Maps during the first quarter of next year to map out the implementation of the resolution.
Dussey said: “To those who say why now, I say, why not? When we look at the world map … it is time for us to change the narrative.”
He added: “It’s time for us in Africa to take responsibility to change what we can change ourselves.”
